For audio LM work, those are more informative than a single aggregate score.89:T5c2,Xiaomi-OCR-0 is a 0.8B VLM initialized from Qwen3.5-0.8B and trained under a unified image–instruction–response interface. The data contains both region-level samples and page-level samples. Region-level samples pair cropped text, table, or formula regions with recognition targets; page-level samples pair full document images with complete parsing targets, including content, structure, and reading order. The data engine has three components. First, an automated annotation pipeline uses PP-DocLayoutV3 to detect semantic regions, then sends crops to a heterogeneous expert pool. High-agreement labels are accepted; lower-agreement cases go through render-guided correction and re-evaluation; unresolved cases are selectively human-verified. The paper introduces Ensemble Triplet Consensus, which combines pool-wide agreement and agreement within a selected three-expert subset to rank candidate labels. Second, multi-factor sample mining uses expert agreement, model self-consistency, and semantic clustering to shape the training mixture. Third, synthetic generation targets coverage gaps and verified failure modes. The training recipe is progressive: Q-Mask-based text anchoring, multi-task continued pretraining, and Mix-RL on hard examples with verifiable rewards. The paper also compares Mix-RL with multi-teacher on-policy distillation, where distillation is more compute-efficient but longer Mix-RL reaches better final parsing and understanding performance.8a:T546,The method has two stages. Stage one is REL-SFT. The authors build a 29.4K Reasoning-Evidence Localization chain-of-thought dataset, where each reasoning trace is aligned with page indices and normalized bounding boxes. Training is done across seven rendering resolutions, so the model learns to localize relevant evidence under compressed global views rather than simply reading everything at high fidelity. Stage two is GRPO. At inference, the model starts from low-DPI page images and iteratively generates a reasoning segment followed by an action: either answer directly or issue a region-enhancement call with a page index and bounding box. A tool then crops the aligned region from a higher-DPI rendering of the same page and returns it as an observation. The model incorporates that observation into subsequent reasoning until it answers or exhausts the call budget. A few design choices matter here: low- and high-resolution views share the same page coordinates, which avoids alignment drift; enhancement is local rather than full-page rerendering, which keeps added visual tokens under control; and policy learning must optimize not only correctness but also when to zoom, where to zoom, and when to stop. The paper also discusses font and point-size selection, highlighting that rendering choices materially affect downstream performance.8b:T446,The strongest results are on compressed long-document reasoning. On RULER v1 at 72 DPI, FocusVTC reaches 87.4 with about 2.9x input compression, compared with 57.5 for Glyph at roughly 3.0x compression. On LongBench, it slightly surpasses its text-input backbone, 56.40 versus 55.86, suggesting that visual compression does not necessarily hurt long-context understanding and may even help through page-level structure plus selective reading. On MRCR, the macro average over six length bins and 2/4/8 needles improves from 31.65 to 45.56, a gain of 13.91, indicating clear benefits in multi-round retrieval and evidence revisiting. The latency evaluation reports a 2.79x online end-to-end speedup on MRCR. On VTCBench, it obtains a 51.19 macro average across Retrieval, Reasoning, and Memory. General multimodal ability is preserved or slightly improved: MMMU rises from 65.12 to 66.73 and MME from 2424.02 to 2457.62. One notable ablation is font choice: at 72 DPI, DejaVu Sans improves LongBench from 54.93 to 56.40 over Verdana, showing that rendering is not a neutral implementation detail.8c:T443,The authors build paired image-to-image and image-to-text tasks that require solving the same visual problem from the same input, differing only in output modality. For instance, an I2I task reconstructs a correctly ordered image from shuffled patches, while the paired I2T task predicts the patch order in text. This design keeps the underlying visual capability fixed and isolates the role of supervision format. They compare six ways of combining I2I and I2T training. The strongest recipe is a two-stage setup: first train on I2I while updating shared parameters, then fine-tune on I2T. Directly mixing I2I and I2T objectives from the beginning does not show the same scaling behavior. The paper then introduces OmniTaskonomy, a shared taxonomy for generation and understanding tasks organized around Recognition, Reconstruction, and Reorganization. Finally, it analyzes task compatibility through gradient alignment, finding that successful transfer is associated with aligned gradients in the understanding branch’s pre-attention normalization parameters, especially in early layers.8d:T441,The experimental evidence has three main components. First, controlled paired-task experiments compare training curricula and show that I2I-before-I2T improves downstream I2T performance, with gains increasing as more I2I data is used. The same setup also shows that I2I supervision reduces the amount of I2T data needed to reach a target understanding performance, especially in low-I2T-data regimes. Second, the OmniTaskonomy transfer map measures source-target relationships between generation tasks and understanding capabilities. Some transfers are expected, such as Z-depth helping metric 3D reasoning and object pointing helping counting. Others are less direct, such as 2.5D segmentation improving category recognition and Z-depth prediction improving localization. Third, gradient analysis shows that I2I and I2T gradients align most strongly in early pre-attention normalization parameters of the understanding branch. Higher mean alignment across generation tasks correlates with larger mean transfer gains, and the same trend appears at the individual source-target-pair level.8e:T4d5,The authors first establish a recipe for training a variable-length 1D ViT tokenizer from scratch, without external distillation. The main contribution is nested self-alignment. Standard nested dropout randomly truncates the latent sequence during training so that prefixes can reconstruct the image, but this often pushes most information into the earliest tokens and leaves tail tokens underused. NesTok adds cross-length training: reconstruction is jointly optimized across multiple token lengths, and shorter-sequence representations are explicitly aligned in latent space to the full-length representation. In effect, the full sequence acts as a semantic anchor. Short prefixes are encouraged not only to reconstruct reasonably well but also to stay semantically close to the full representation, while later tokens are left to refine details progressively. Importantly, the framework stays within a discrete 1D tokenizer plus ViT decoder plus standard next-token AR generation pipeline. The gains therefore come from better tokenizer learning rather than from switching to a more complex diffusion or flow decoder. The paper also analyzes codebook entropy and utilization, showing that self-alignment mitigates tail-token collapse.8f:T8bf,The method is built around a reverse-SFT pipeline followed by semantic-consistency RL. The system is formalized as a prompt enhancer πθ feeding a video generator Gϕ. The goal is to generate a textual condition y that is easier for Gϕ to realize faithfully. Instead of starting from a user request x and expanding it forward into a richer prompt, WanPE starts from a high-quality real video v, derives a hierarchical cinematic condition y from that video, and then reconstructs a compatible but information-sparser user request x. The pair (x, y) is used for supervised training. The motivation is straightforward: y is grounded in real video and therefore better aligned with the conditioning distribution seen by the generator, while x approximates realistic user input at inference time.

The hierarchical cinematic condition appears to be organized at the shot level rather than as a single long paragraph. It captures scene setup, entities, actions, camera language, lighting, audio or dialogue, and narrative progression across shots. This matters because cinematic planning is a coupled control problem: action, camera, pacing, editing, and atmosphere evolve together and cannot be handled well by local prompt embellishment.

After SFT, the model is optimized with SC-GRPO. The key contribution here is the reward design rather than GRPO itself. The paper defines a nine-dimensional semantic-consistency reward to check whether user requirements are preserved across the entire plan. The reward targets omissions, semantic drift, incorrect bindings between entities and attributes or actions, and temporal inconsistencies across shots. Compared with rewards based only on fluency or overall text quality, this is much closer to structured fidelity. In effect, the RL stage acts like a global verifier for long-form planning: the model is encouraged not only to sound cinematic, but to remain faithful to the original request throughout the generated plan.

Another notable point is transferability. The authors claim WanPE can transfer across video generators after format adaptation. That suggests the model is learning a more abstract planning representation rather than memorizing a single generator-specific prompt template.90:T806,Three parts of the experimental section matter most. First is scale and headline gain. The paper trains WanPE variants from 4B to 397B on 1.05M real-world videos. According to the reported main results, WanPE-397B improves over raw prompts by up to 18.84 points for 5–15 second generation and 50.86 points for 30-second generation. The larger gain at longer duration is important: it suggests the value of prompt planning grows with temporal horizon because longer videos depend more heavily on front-end structure.

Second is the ablation evidence. Reverse construction outperforms forward rewriting, which supports the paper’s central claim that distribution alignment to real video-grounded conditions matters more than simply making prompts more descriptive. SC-GRPO improves semantic consistency by 18.6 to 23.3 points across scales. That is a substantial effect size and indicates that the main bottleneck in long-form prompt planning is requirement preservation, not surface-level wording. If the full paper breaks down reward dimensions such as omission, binding, and temporal consistency, those tables are worth reading carefully because they reveal what kinds of failures RL is actually fixing.

Third is evaluation design. The authors build WanPEval, a human-annotated benchmark covering 5 to 30 seconds and varying intent granularity, and evaluate both at the text level and through roughly 11K blind pairwise video comparisons. That is stronger than text-only evaluation because the real utility of a prompt enhancer must show up in generated video. The paper also reports that WanPE leads evaluated commercial offerings at 5–15 seconds and remains competitive with Seedance 2.5 at 30 seconds. This suggests the method is already effective in medium-duration settings, while very long generation is still partly capped by the downstream generator. If transfer experiments across generators are included in detail, those are especially useful for judging whether the model learned general planning or platform-specific prompting habits.91:T4cc,For a quick but useful read, focus on three places. First, read the introduction carefully where the paper argues that forward rewriting and video-grounded conditioning come from different distributions. That section determines whether the work is merely a large engineering system or a genuine task reformulation. Second, inspect the method section for the exact structure of the hierarchical cinematic condition and how reverse construction builds training pairs from real videos. If that pipeline is weak, much of the gain may simply come from model scale. Third, study the SC-GRPO reward design and its ablations, especially what each of the nine reward dimensions measures and whether the training remains stable.

In the experiments, prioritize: (1) comparisons among raw prompts, forward baselines, reverse-SFT, and reverse+SC-GRPO across different video lengths; (2) scaling behavior from 4B to 397B; (3) whether text-level gains match video-level blind preference; and (4) transfer across generators. A solid skim should take about 30 to 45 minutes. If only one part is worth deeper inspection, make it the reverse-construction data pipeline and the semantic-consistency reward, since those are the most reusable ideas.92:T4dd,The method, called action forcing, starts from pixel displacement tracks across frames. Since similar egomotion directions induce recurring coherent motion patterns in the image plane, the authors run PCA over these displacement vectors and use the leading components as an egomotion basis. The first two component weights are used as low-dimensional action inputs. This avoids conditioning on dense flow or raw tracks at inference time, and it gives the action space an explicit affine structure: zero means no egomotion, scalar magnitude controls strength, sign controls direction, and axes can be combined. The world model is built by adapting a pretrained video DiT, specifically Wan2.1, under a conditional flow matching objective. The model learns a velocity field between noise latents and clean video latents, and the action is injected into the velocity network itself. This is different from applying a fixed transformation after generation; the action can shape the latent trajectory and the scene evolution. The paper also introduces an online latent egomotion critic that distills pixel-space motion into differentiable latent supervision, grounding action following without backpropagating through the video decoder or the tracker.93:T62b,The method has three main components. First, a physical mechanism interpreter maps each action-outcome branch to a distribution over latent mechanisms rather than a point estimate. This matters because different interventions constrain the underlying physics to different degrees: a strong push may sharply identify friction, while a weak interaction may leave many mechanisms plausible. Second, the paper introduces a shared-world evidence score. Instead of forcing branch posteriors to be identical, it measures whether all branches retain common support for a shared mechanism relative to an initial-scene prior p(z|I0). The prior correction is important: it prevents uninformative branches from appearing falsely consistent simply because they remain broad and uncertain. Third, the learned compatibility signal is injected into both training and sampling. The interpreter is trained using same-world groups versus mismatched-world groups, then frozen. Its evidence score is used during flow training and also as sampling-time guidance, so the generated rollouts are nudged toward sets of futures that admit one common physical explanation. A key design choice is weak coupling: the model does not force videos or latent posteriors to collapse to the same representation, only to remain jointly explainable by one mechanism. For evaluation, the paper defines the shared-world gap: fit physical parameters separately for each branch, then fit one shared parameter set jointly across branches; the extra error under the shared fit quantifies inconsistency across interventions.94:T454,Experiments are conducted in three controlled physical environments: Push Cube, Push Rope, and Pour Water, covering rigid-body, deformable, and particle-based dynamics. The main baseline is ACWM-DiT under the ACWM-Phys interaction setup. Relative to ACWM-DiT, OneWorld reduces the mean shared-world gap by 84.3%, which is the central result, and also improves mean M-MSE by about 7.7×10^-4, suggesting that consistency gains do not come at the expense of ordinary rollout quality. The most convincing part of the empirical section is the separation between single-branch plausibility and multi-branch physical compatibility: some baseline predictions fit physics reasonably well branch by branch, but fail badly once a single shared physical configuration is required. The paper also highlights the role of distributional mechanism inference, same-world versus mismatched-world interpreter training, and the use of the compatibility signal at both training and sampling time. The contribution is less about scale and more about closing the loop between formulation, training signal, and evaluation protocol.95:T4a2,PreviewDiff is a training-free inference-time method for pretrained image and video diffusion models. It treats intermediate denoised latent estimates as search states. At selected denoising checkpoints, the latent is decoded into a preview and passed to a multimodal judge. The judge produces a prompt-satisfaction estimate and natural-language corrective feedback. The feedback may identify missing objects, wrong attributes, incorrect counts, violated spatial relations, or temporal inconsistencies. These critiques are converted into semantic search actions through alternative correction prompts, local re-noising restarts, and latent continuations. Candidate branches are scored, pruned, and rolled forward with a beam-style tree search. Compared with Best-of-N, the method can intervene before generation is complete and reuse partial computation. Compared with scalar reward-guided diffusion, it uses the judge as both a value estimator and a policy-like proposer of semantic fixes. Compared with video-specific tree methods such as Video-T1, it searches over corrected diffusion latent continuations rather than only over final candidates or autoregressive frame continuations.96:T425,Rollout-Marginal Distillation keeps the autoregressive rollout mechanism unchanged: the generator still predicts each new chunk conditioned on its generated history. The change is in the teacher signal. Video-level DMD minimizes a reverse KL between the noised student rollout distribution and a pretrained teacher video distribution, using the difference between a frozen real score and an online fake score. RMD instead scores each generated chunk independently, without exposing the teacher to the imperfect history or future chunks. The objective matches the student’s chunk marginal distribution to a teacher-defined chunk distribution. The chunk teacher is prepared by adapting a video diffusion model on individual chunks extracted from videos generated by the original bidirectional model. Since independent chunk scoring does not enforce cross-chunk relations, the method adds a later video-level DMD refinement stage to improve temporal transitions. No generator architecture changes, fixed anchors, frame sinks, or explicit memory modules are used.97:T613,The method is Prompt-Enhanced On-Policy Self-Distillation (PE-OPSD). Let p be the raw prompt and p+ the enhanced prompt produced by an external Prompt Enhancer. The student is conditioned only on p, while the teacher is conditioned on p+. Training proceeds on the student’s own on-policy flow trajectory: the student generates states under raw-prompt conditioning, and at those visited states the teacher provides target vector fields computed under the enhanced prompt. The student then matches those targets.

Two design choices matter. First, supervision is applied to the flow dynamics rather than only to final samples or to newly constructed text-image pairs. This is why the paper distinguishes itself from SFT-style alternatives: it does not require rebuilding the dataset around enhanced prompts. Second, the asymmetry is only in the conditioning signal, not in the task family. Teacher and student live in the same flow-matching framework, so the distilled object is: given the same latent state, how would a better-informed condition change the denoising or transport direction?

The paper positions this as on-policy self-distillation, where the teacher can be a stop-gradient or EMA view rather than a separately trained external model. The critical comparison is against three baselines: inference-time prompt enhancement, SFT with enhanced prompts, and off-policy distillation. The claimed advantage is that PE-OPSD removes inference-time overhead while aligning supervision with the states the raw-prompt student will actually encounter.98:T64e,From the provided full-text excerpt, the experimental message is clear even though many exact numbers are not visible. The paper reports that PE-OPSD outperforms three baseline families on aggregate prompt fidelity across three main flow-matching backbones: 1) inference-time Prompt Enhancer, 2) SFT, and 3) off-policy distillation. It also preserves positive changes in visual appeal while keeping base-model inference latency, since both the Prompt Enhancer and the teacher are removed at deployment.

The evaluation setup is well chosen for the claim being made. Comparison to inference-time PE tests whether the external module can be internalized. Comparison to SFT tests whether simply training on expanded text conditions is enough. Comparison to off-policy distillation tests whether state-distribution alignment is the real driver.

The most important expected ablations are: on-policy versus off-policy supervision, raw versus enhanced teacher conditioning, EMA/shared-teacher variants, consistency across backbones, and stratification by prompt underspecification. The introduction already states the main findings: on-policy beats off-policy, suggesting state alignment matters; PE-OPSD beats SFT, suggesting static text replacement is not equivalent to dynamic trajectory supervision; and it beats inference-time PE on aggregate prompt fidelity, suggesting the model has indeed absorbed part of the enhanced-prompt behavior.

The excerpt does not expose the full tables, exact backbone names, parameter counts, or absolute gains, so those should be checked in the original paper before citing numbers.99:T440,This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction and make sure the problem framing is clear: the goal is not to build a better prompt rewriter, but to absorb the rewriter’s benefit into the generator. Then read the method section around the on-policy self-distillation objective. The key idea is simple and worth understanding: supervise the student on the states it actually visits.

In the experiments, prioritize three comparisons: PE-OPSD versus inference-time PE, versus SFT, and versus off-policy distillation. If those three hold, the paper’s core claim is established. For ablations, focus on short or underspecified prompts, attribute binding, and compositional prompts, since those are the cases where prompt enhancement should matter most.

A practical reading budget is about 20–30 minutes. The deeper question worth carrying forward is whether this privileged-condition on-policy distillation pattern can transfer to language models—for example, using retrieval, chain-of-thought, or verifier signals only during training while keeping inference-time inputs minimal.9a:Tac4,方法上最重要的是“串行阶段化 + 奖励硬度排序 + 难度过滤”。完整流水线是 SFT → Reasoning RL → Coding RL → Instruction-Following RL → General Agent → Coding Agent → Search Agent → RLHF，全部基于同一个 GLM-4.5-Air-Base（106B total / 12B active）连续更新参数。

第一部分是 SFT。作者把它当成 capability-building stage，而不是格式对齐。SFT 的作用有两个：一是建立广泛能力下限，二是统一输出格式，尤其是 native <think> chat format 和多轮交互模板。这里隐含的判断是，如果 SFT 没把能力面铺开，后续 RL 只能在狭窄分布上做局部修补，容易出现 reward overfitting。

第二部分是多阶段 RL。Reasoning RL 和 Coding RL 先做，因为奖励最硬，分别依赖可验证答案或执行/测试信号，属于 RLVR。Instruction-Following RL 虽然用了 rubric-based judge，但被放在 agent 阶段之前，因为作者观察到 instruction following 离模型原有聊天能力更近，judge 可被利用的空间较小。General/Coding/Search Agent 三个阶段再把工具使用、环境交互和长轨迹决策加进来。最后才做 RLHF，用偏好型软奖励去修整开放式质量。

第三部分是 difficulty filtering。作者反复强调，训练样本要落在“可学但未掌握”的区间：已经会做的 prompt 要丢掉，大多数阶段里始终不会做的 prompt 也丢掉。这样做不是简单提纯数据，而是在 on-policy RL 中构造自动 curriculum，避免梯度浪费在零优势样本或纯噪声样本上。相比只按题目元数据分桶，这种基于当前策略表现的过滤更贴近真实学习边界。

第四部分是基础设施设计。作者明确指出，多轮 agent RL 需要 token-in/token-out rollouts，也就是把模型生成和环境返回都作为在线轨迹的一部分，而不是离线拼接。为了稳定 RL，他们使用大 batch 和 Rollout Routing Replay；后者的作用是缓解长轨迹、多环境、异步 rollout 带来的分布抖动。另一个关键点是从 SFT 到 agent 阶段保持 chat template 一致，避免模板漂移把能力变化和格式变化混在一起。对于 coding/search agent，还需要长时间稳定运行的 sandbox/service，否则 reward 噪声会直接污染策略更新。

和常见做法相比，这篇工作的区别不在单个算法，而在把“为什么先做这个、后做那个”讲得很具体。很多工作把 IF、agent、RLHF 混在一起做多目标优化；这里则明确按 reward 可验证性和被攻击风险排序。很多工作也做 hard example mining，但这里是按当前 policy 的成功带宽做动态过滤，更接近 RL 里的 learnability control。9b:T927,The central design is a serial pipeline with explicit stage responsibilities, reward-hardness ordering, and difficulty filtering. The full sequence is SFT → Reasoning RL → Coding RL → Instruction-Following RL → General Agent → Coding Agent → Search Agent → RLHF, all applied to the same GLM-4.5-Air-Base checkpoint (106B total, 12B active MoE).

SFT is treated as the capability foundation. Its role is not only to align output style, but to establish broad competence and normalize the model’s interaction format, including the native <think> template and multi-turn chat behavior. The implicit claim is that if SFT does not already cover the capability surface, later RL will overfit narrow reward channels rather than build robust skills.

The RL stages are ordered by reward reliability. Reasoning RL and Coding RL come first because they rely on hard verification signals such as exact answers, execution, or tests. Instruction-Following RL uses a rubric-based judge, but it is still placed before the agent stages because instruction following is close to the model’s native chat behavior and therefore less exposed to severe reward gaming. General Agent, Coding Agent, and Search Agent then introduce tool use and environment interaction. RLHF is deliberately last, since open-ended preference rewards are the easiest to exploit.

A key mechanism is difficulty filtering. The training prompts are restricted to a productive band: prompts the current policy already solves are removed, and in most stages prompts it never solves are also removed. This turns on-policy RL into an automatic curriculum over learnable examples. Compared with static hard-example mining, the filter is policy-dependent and tracks the current learning frontier.

The infrastructure section is unusually important. The authors use token-in/token-out rollouts for multi-turn on-policy RL, large batches for stability, and Rollout Routing Replay to reduce variance and distributional jitter from long trajectories and asynchronous environments. They also emphasize strict chat-template consistency from SFT through agent stages, plus reliable sandbox services for long coding and search episodes. The paper’s novelty is less about a new optimizer or reward formula, and more about making the sequencing logic and systems constraints explicit.9c:T5b0,The most useful experimental contribution is the stagewise analysis rather than the final leaderboard. The final Rufus-Air model outperforms the official GLM-4.5-Air release on every reported benchmark except Arena-Hard v2 Creative Writing, and is competitive with similarly sized open models such as INTELLECT-3 and Nemotron-3-Super. It leads on instruction-following and most alignment and agentic rows, ties Nemotron-3-Super on Terminal-Bench 2.1, trails on a few Tau2 domain rows, and is weaker on creative writing.

More importantly, each stage is evaluated against the checkpoint it starts from, not only against the final model. That design is critical in multi-stage post-training because later stages overwrite the same parameters. Without stagewise comparisons, it is hard to tell whether a gain comes from the intended stage or from accidental carryover.

The paper’s main empirical claims are that strong SFT materially raises the downstream ceiling, Reasoning RL improves not only reasoning tasks but also later instruction-following, and difficulty filtering is a major driver of stable RL gains. The excerpt already gives the practical scale: the RL stages run on 8 to 32 nodes with a 12B-active MoE model, which makes the recipe accessible outside frontier labs. When reading the full paper, the most reusable numbers are likely in the stagewise tables, the filtering ratios, and the compute table rather than the final benchmark summary.9d:T432,Start with the Introduction and Recipe Overview. The four claims to anchor on are: SFT builds capability, difficulty filtering creates an automatic curriculum, stage order should follow reward reliability, and infrastructure is part of the recipe.

Then read the per-stage sections carefully, especially the data, reward, and filtering rules. The key question is not just what data they used, but why each capability is trained at that point in the pipeline rather than earlier or later. The placement of Reasoning RL before IF RL, and RLHF at the very end, deserves close attention.

Do not skip the infrastructure section. For anyone working on agent RL or long-horizon post-training, this is where much of the practical value sits: token-in/token-out rollouts, template consistency, sandbox reliability, large-batch RL, and Rollout Routing Replay.

Finally, read the benchmark and ablation tables with a stagewise lens. Focus on Figure 1, Table 1, Table 2, and Table 16. A careful read should take around 1.5 to 2.5 hours; a recipe-only pass can be done in under an hour.9e:T8fc,整体框架分三层：大规模多模态 SFT 打底，IDRL 做核心后训练，PAH 做系统层外循环优化。

第一层是 SFT。Pistis-27B 和 9B 分别建立在 Qwen3.6 与 Qwen3.5 基座上。Thinking 版本用结构化 reasoning 数据做大规模多模态 SFT，Agentic 版本则进一步加入 agentic trajectories，覆盖长程规划、迭代推理、工具使用以及文本/图像混合场景。这里的作用是提供一个足够好的 cold start，因为文中明确提到 on-policy distillation 对初始 student-teacher overlap 敏感，没有合适起点时容易失败。

第二层是 IDRL。它不是把 distillation loss 和 RL loss 静态加权求和，也不是先蒸馏后 RL 的串行流程，而是在同一训练循环中交替执行 on-policy distillation 更新和 RL 更新。on-policy distillation 的对象是学生自己采样出来的序列，再用教师分布提供 token-level 密集监督；RL 则继续根据任务回报优化策略。作者的论点是：如果两种目标放在同一次更新里，会出现梯度干扰；如果完全分阶段，又失去相互校正的机会。交替更新相当于在时间上解耦目标冲突，同时保留动态互动。文中把收益归因于三点：探索更充分、策略熵保持更好、优化更稳定。

对于 agentic 长轨迹，作者再加了 PAS，step-level positive-advantage suppression。它针对的问题是 trajectory-level reward 的常见偏差：一条轨迹最后成功了，中间一些无效甚至错误的动作也可能因为共享正 advantage 而被错误强化。PAS 的做法是对这些中间步骤的正优势进行抑制，避免“搭便车式”信用分配。虽然从摘要信息看不到精确公式，但思想很清楚：不是所有位于成功轨迹上的动作都应得到正反馈。

第三层是 Pistis-Auto-Harnessing。它不改模型参数，也不改工具接口，而是用一个 Optimization Agent 基于开发集轨迹提出、验证并筛选 harness revision，例如工作流、prompt、技能调用、证据表示和路由逻辑的调整。只有在开发指标上确实变好时才保留修改，然后冻结到评测阶段。这个设计把“学策略”和“调系统”分开，减少了把系统工程收益误记到模型能力上的风险。9f:Ta42,The framework has three layers: large-scale multimodal SFT for initialization, IDRL for core post-training, and PAH for system-level outer-loop optimization.

The first layer is SFT. Pistis-27B and Pistis-9B are built on Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 respectively. The Thinking variants are trained on structured multimodal reasoning data, while the Agentic variants additionally include agentic trajectories covering long-horizon planning, iterative reasoning, tool use, and mixed text-vision interaction. This stage is important because the paper explicitly notes that on-policy distillation is sensitive to student-teacher overlap and can fail without a strong cold start.

The second layer is IDRL. Instead of using a static weighted sum of distillation and RL losses, or running distillation and RL as separate stages, IDRL alternates between on-policy distillation updates and RL updates within a single training loop. In the distillation step, the student is trained against the teacher distribution on student-generated sequences, giving dense token-level supervision. In the RL step, the policy is optimized against task reward. The motivation is that a static joint loss can create objective interference within the same update, while a purely staged pipeline prevents the two signals from interacting during training. Interleaving is meant to decouple the objectives in time while still allowing them to shape the same evolving policy. The claimed benefits are better exploration, higher retained policy entropy, and more stable optimization.

For long-horizon agentic training, the paper adds PAS, or step-level positive-advantage suppression. This targets a common failure mode in trajectory-level RL: if a trajectory succeeds overall, some ineffective or even wrong intermediate actions may still receive positive credit because they share the trajectory’s positive advantage. PAS suppresses positive advantage on such steps, reducing this hitchhiking effect. The exact formula is not visible from the provided text, but the intent is clear: not every action on a successful trajectory deserves reinforcement.

The third layer is Pistis-Auto-Harnessing. PAH does not change the policy weights or the tool interface. Instead, an Optimization Agent proposes bounded revisions to the inference harness using development trajectories, validates them against a development metric, and keeps only those revisions that improve the metric. The selected harness is then frozen for evaluation. This cleanly separates model learning from workflow optimization, including prompts, skills, evidence representation, and routing logic.a0:T731,The experimental story has two main tracks: Thinking models and Agentic models. For Thinking, Pistis-27B-Thinking is roughly on par with Qwen3.8-27B on 24 non-grounding benchmarks, 82.3 versus 82.4, while reaching the highest grounding average of 80.5, which is 8.6 points above Qwen3.8-27B. That is a useful result because it suggests the post-training recipe improves grounding substantially without sacrificing general reasoning. The 9B Thinking model is reported to achieve the best averages among similarly sized models on both benchmark groups.

For Agentic models, the gains over the corresponding base models are more pronounced on long-horizon interactive tasks. Relative to Qwen3.6-27B, Pistis-27B-Agentic improves BrowseComp-VL, MMSearch, VDR-testmini, and LiveVQA by 8.8, 3.3, 3.2, and 9.7 points. Relative to Qwen3.5-9B, Pistis-9B-Agentic improves the same tasks by 8.4, 8.0, 3.2, and 11.4 points. The larger gains on multimodal search and live interaction are consistent with the paper’s claim that IDRL and agentic trajectory training are especially helpful for long-horizon decision-making rather than single-turn QA.

The ablation section is likely where the paper is most informative. The authors state that IDRL outperforms pure on-policy distillation, pure RL, and a static joint objective. If the full report includes training curves, the most useful things to inspect are whether validation metrics are smoother, whether policy entropy decays more slowly, and whether the interleaving schedule matters. For PAS, the key question is whether it reduces the rate of bad intermediate actions inside successful trajectories and whether it improves sample efficiency on long-horizon tasks. For PAH, the important evidence is how much gain comes from harness optimization alone under the same environment-interaction budget.a1:T4b4,A good skim should follow the order: method first, system second, results third. Start with the definition of IDRL and the training-loop diagram. The main thing to verify is the granularity of interleaving: whether it happens at the update level, batch level, or in larger alternating phases. That determines how different it really is from prior distillation-plus-RL pipelines. Then read the PAS formulation or pseudocode to see whether it is implemented through masking, clipping, or a more selective step filter. After that, inspect PAH, not just for the score gains but for how it avoids contaminating evaluation and how clearly it separates harness changes from policy learning.

In the experiments, prioritize: (1) the main ablation comparing IDRL against OPD, RL, and static joint training; (2) training stability and entropy curves; (3) consistency across 27B and 9B scales for both Thinking and Agentic variants; and (4) the standalone contribution of PAH with a fixed model. A useful skim should take about 35 to 50 minutes. If only one part deserves deeper attention, make it the IDRL interleaving mechanism and the PAS credit-assignment treatment, since those are the most transferable ideas.a2:T4b6,The proposed method, GRAFT, stands for Graph-based Faithful Step-level credit assignment. It reorganizes multiple rollout trajectories from the same prompt into a trajectory graph instead of treating them as isolated chains. Nodes represent states and edges represent actions. State canonicalization merges identical or semantically similar states using exact matching or embedding-based similarity. The outgoing actions from a merged node then form an on-state action group, which is closer to the group required by the standard advantage definition. The method estimates node values by Bellman-style propagation over the graph using only terminal outcome rewards. Given these values, the step advantage is defined as A_t = gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t). The paper also introduces Graph GAE, extending generalized advantage estimation to the trajectory graph by aggregating multi-hop future advantage estimates. Compared with PRM-based approaches, GRAFT does not require step-level reward annotation. Compared with group normalization by step index, it avoids mixing different states into one baseline. Compared with resampling continuations from every intermediate state, it avoids the O(N^2 T) rollout cost.a3:T430,SLCA-GRPO introduces Segment-Locked Credit Assignment. The rollout is first segmented with masks: environment tokens are excluded from policy gradients, and learnable policy tokens are split into a tool segment and a summary segment. The final contiguous learnable block is treated as the summary segment; all earlier learnable blocks, including reasoning traces and structured tool calls, form the tool segment. The method then computes separate group-relative advantages for tool-side and summary-side rewards. During optimization, tool advantages are routed only to tool tokens, and summary advantages only to summary tokens. This blocks cross-segment advantage contamination before backpropagation, without extra rollouts and without separating the agent into planner and summarizer models. Hierarchical Rewards provide segment-level feedback, and a Schema-Guided LLM Simulator supplies scalable tool-interaction rollouts. Unlike VinePPO, SPO, or GiGPO, which mainly operate along the temporal axis, SLCA operates along a structural execution-versus-articulation axis.a4:T409,The paper formalizes an agent episode as a sequence of model actions and environment observations, with a binary outcome reward assigned at the end. It builds on GRPO, where multiple trajectories are sampled per task and group-relative advantages are computed from their rewards. The criticized OPSD setup conditions the same model on privileged context to obtain a stronger teacher distribution, then asks the ordinary student view to match it. This creates an irreducible information mismatch. Privileged Self-Practice changes where the privileged information is used. If the model’s rollouts on a task mostly fail, an analyzer model writes a short task-specific instruction. The system then resamples a guided group with that instruction in context. Guided and unguided groups are scored under their own sampling contexts, and advantages are computed within each group. The same GRPO objective is used; there is no loss term comparing the privileged and non-privileged views. At inference time, the extra instruction is removed.a5:T989,方法核心是 CounterRoute，一个在线 RL 框架，直接从原生支持 thinking / no-thinking 的单一 checkpoint 出发训练，不额外做该方法专用的 SFT warm-up，也不引入外部 router。形式化上，策略先对给定 prompt 采样模式 m∈{TH, NT}，再在该模式下生成回答 z。论文定义了带效率边际 b 的路由目标：只有当 thinking 的估计效用比 no-thinking 高出至少 b 时，才值得走 TH；否则优先走更便宜的 NT。这个 b 不是 token 成本的显式建模，而是 reward space 里的偏置，用来避免在两种模式质量接近时无谓思考。

训练上有两个关键设计。其一是 paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts。对一部分 prompt，强制当前策略分别在 TH 和 NT 下各生成一次回答，得到同一 prompt 下的成对反事实样本。然后比较两种模式的 utility，构造跨模式 credit。因为两条回答都来自当前策略，而不是旧策略、规则标签或外部教师，所以路由监督会随着策略能力一起更新，缓解 non-stationary target 问题。

其二是 hierarchical counterfactual credit assignment。论文采用一种“分离式 token 级赋值”规则：在最初的路由 token 上，不使用模式内 advantage，而是用经过截断或边界控制的跨模式 utility 差值来替换；在后续回答 token 上，只用该模式内部的 GRPO 优势做更新。这样路由 token 学的是“选 TH 还是 NT”，回答 token 学的是“在已选模式下怎么答得更好”，两类梯度不再混在一起。相比把整条序列统一做 policy gradient，这种做法更贴合层级决策结构。

第三个设计是 paired-to-self-routed curriculum。训练早期，为了避免初始模式偏好压制探索，模型会保留较高比例的 paired prompts，让两种模式都持续被采样并获得训练信号；随后逐步过渡到 self-routed prompts，让模型自己决定模式。这个 curriculum 的作用不是提升最终上限，而是稳定 co-learning 过程，避免一开始就被单一模式锁死。

从全文描述看，论文还强调它与 Thinkless、HGPO、TON 等方法的区别：这些方法通常先做额外的双模式 SFT 或混合微调，再用 RL 学路由；CounterRoute 则试图直接从现成 dual-mode checkpoint 出发，用在线 RL 同时学路由和两种回答策略，减少对 warm-up 数据分布的依赖。a6:T8a4,实验主体在 Qwen3-8B 和 Qwen3-14B 上进行。训练数据只用数学和合成 instruction-following prompts，但评测覆盖 9 个 held-out benchmark，包含 reasoning、coding、knowledge、commonsense 和 instruction following。主结果是：Qwen3-8B 的宏平均准确率达到 79.1%，Qwen3-14B 达到 82.4%，都优于同数据训练的 Think-Only GRPO，同时平均生成 token 更少。相对各自的 always-thinking checkpoint，CounterRoute 在 8B 上把平均生成 token 降低 51%，在 14B 上降低 41%，同时准确率还有提升。这说明它不是单纯靠少想来省算力，而是在不少简单样本上学会了直接答，并把节省下来的训练与推理预算转化成了更好的整体策略。

论文还给出一个很关键的现象：在 direct answering 本来就强的 benchmark 上，学到的 think rate 可以低到 1%，而 direct-answer 能力本身还会继续提升。这意味着 NT 分支不是被动保留，而是在 RL 中被单独训练得更强。另一个有价值的分析是 same-checkpoint forced-mode evaluation：对同一个训练后的 checkpoint，分别强制 TH 和 NT 作答，再看两者性能差与模型实际学到的 think rate 是否一致。结果显示，在 held-out 的 coding、science、knowledge、commonsense 上，think rate 大体跟随“thinking 相对 direct 的经验收益”变化，尽管这些域并不在 RL 训练混合中。这说明路由策略学到的不是简单的表面模式，而是某种可迁移的价值判断。

消融主要在 Qwen3-8B 上做，重点验证四个组件：反事实成对采样、模式分离的回答优化、效率边际 b、以及 paired-to-self-routed curriculum。摘要和正文给出的结论是，这四项都对稳定训练和最终的 accuracy/token trade-off 有贡献。尤其是去掉成对反事实或去掉分离式 credit assignment 时，路由更容易被回答质量噪声污染；去掉 curriculum 时，早期模式偏好更容易自我强化，导致探索不足。由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格数值，无法逐项复述所有 ablation 的具体百分点，但主结论是组件作用比较清楚，不是单一技巧堆出来的结果。a7:T8f9,CounterRoute starts from an off-the-shelf native dual-mode checkpoint, such as Qwen3, and trains everything with online RL, without method-specific SFT warm-up, routing labels, an external router, or separate models. Formally, the policy first samples a mode m in {TH, NT} for a prompt x, then generates a response z conditioned on x and m. The routing objective is defined with an efficiency margin b: thinking is preferred only if its estimated utility exceeds no-thinking by at least b; ties go to NT. This margin is a reward-space prior that biases toward the cheaper mode when quality is similar.

The first key mechanism is paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts. For selected prompts, the current policy is forced to answer once in TH and once in NT. This produces paired responses under both modes for the same prompt, allowing direct cross-mode utility comparison. Because both rollouts come from the current policy, the routing target tracks the model’s evolving capabilities instead of relying on fixed labels, heuristics, or a teacher.

The second mechanism is hierarchical counterfactual credit assignment. The paper uses a disjoint token-level rule. At the initial routing token, the usual within-mode advantage is replaced by a bounded cross-mode utility credit. For the response tokens, only within-mode GRPO advantage is used. This means the routing token learns which mode to choose, while the response tokens learn how to answer well within the chosen mode. Compared with sequence-level policy gradients over the whole output, this better matches the hierarchical structure of the decision process.

The third mechanism is a paired-to-self-routed curriculum. Early in training, the method keeps enough paired prompts so both modes continue to receive evidence and updates. Later, control is gradually transferred to autonomous self-routing. The purpose is to prevent early mode bias from collapsing exploration before the value of both modes is estimated reliably.

Relative to prior adaptive-reasoning methods such as Thinkless, HGPO, and TON, the paper’s main distinction is that it does not rely on extra dual-mode SFT or hybrid fine-tuning before RL. It tries to co-learn routing and both conditional response policies directly from a native dual-mode checkpoint.a8:T792,The main experiments use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B. RL training uses only math and synthetic instruction-following prompts, while evaluation spans nine held-out benchmarks covering reasoning, coding, knowledge, commonsense, and instruction following. The headline result is a macro-average accuracy of 79.1% for Qwen3-8B and 82.4% for Qwen3-14B. Both outperform same-data Think-Only GRPO while using fewer generated tokens on average. Relative to the corresponding always-thinking checkpoints, CounterRoute reduces mean generated tokens by 51% on 8B and 41% on 14B, while also improving accuracy.

A notable result is that on benchmarks where direct answering is already strong, the learned think rate can drop to as low as 1%, and the direct-answer branch still improves. That suggests the NT branch is not merely preserved for efficiency; it is actively trained into a stronger policy. Another important analysis is the same-checkpoint forced-mode evaluation. The trained checkpoint is evaluated once with forced TH and once with forced NT, and the empirical benefit of thinking is compared with the learned think rate. The paper reports that think rates broadly track the actual value of reasoning across held-out coding, science, knowledge, and commonsense domains, even though those domains are absent from the RL training mixture. That is a stronger sign of route-value alignment than raw benchmark averages alone.

Ablations are reported on Qwen3-8B and cover the main components: paired counterfactual rollouts, mode-separated response optimization, the efficiency margin, and the paired-to-self-routed curriculum. The qualitative conclusion is that each component matters for stability and for the final accuracy-versus-token trade-off. The provided text does not include all table values, so not every ablation delta can be quoted here, but the paper does present controlled evidence rather than relying on a single aggregate gain.a9:T516,For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, read the introduction and problem formulation to understand why routing is treated as a hierarchical decision rather than a static classifier, and how the efficiency margin b is defined. Second, read the method section around paired counterfactual rollouts and token-level credit assignment. The central idea is simple but easy to miss: routing tokens get cross-mode credit, response tokens get within-mode GRPO. Third, read the same-checkpoint forced-mode analysis, because that is where the paper shows whether routing actually tracks the value of reasoning.

If time is limited, the system overview figure, training algorithm, main results table, think-rate plots, and ablation table should be enough to grasp the contribution in about 25 to 35 minutes. For deeper reading, two questions are worth keeping in mind. One is whether this credit decomposition extends beyond binary TH/NT routing to multiple reasoning budgets. The other is whether the current reward-space efficiency margin can be replaced by a more explicit model of token cost, latency, or tool cost. A further pretraining-facing question is whether native dual-mode separability should be encouraged earlier, during pretraining or mid-training, rather than learned only at the RL stage.aa:T437,The central object is the conditional proof-difficulty function V(T|P), the difficulty of proving a target theorem T given an available premise set P. Lean 4 and mathlib provide the formal environment, and proof difficulty is operationalized through formal proof length or proof cost. Using the dependency structure in mathlib, the authors post-train a 27B model to predict V(T|P) before the proof is actually constructed. They then define intrinsic interestingness as proof length divided by statement length. The intended signal is high information density: a theorem that is short to state but hard to prove is more interesting. They also define utility as the amount by which adding a theorem to the mathematical context compresses later proofs. Utility captures reusable abstraction, while interestingness is easier to estimate locally. The paper reports a strong correlation between the two, which motivates using interestingness as a practical reward. The metric is then used both for post-training theorem generation and for inference-time pruning in recursive discovery.ab:T56b,The paper first characterizes the failure of OPRD-style methods, then proposes LastOPD. In the baseline recipe, the student rolls out its own responses, the teacher scores them, and latent supervision is added by pairing student and teacher layers at matched relative depth, with a projector bridging hidden-size differences. The authors argue that this setup has two structural problems. First, depth-matched layers need not play the same functional role. Their J-Lens analysis shows that the teacher’s final answer becomes readable mainly in the last two layers, whereas the student’s answer emerges more gradually across layers. Second, common alignment metrics can be dominated by a few large dimensions, so improving similarity scores may not reflect useful functional matching. LastOPD changes the recipe in three ways. It aligns only the final hidden states immediately before the LM heads, avoiding intermediate layer pairing altogether. It uses a small trainable MLP to bridge width differences at that final interface. And it treats latent supervision as a short-lived scaffold: over the first 10 steps, the latent loss is linearly decayed while a token-level reverse top-k loss is linearly increased, after which training continues with token-only OPD. The key idea is that latent supervision is useful as an early directional signal but harmful when kept active too long.ac:T595,The main setup distills Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B teachers into Qwen3-1.7B-Base using DAPO-Math-17k, with MATH-500 as the main validation benchmark. The collapse is striking. In the 4B-to-1.7B setting, latent-only OPRD raises MATH-500 from 25.4 to 46.2 within 10 steps, outperforming vanilla OPD by 28 points at that stage. But continued optimization drives the score down to 11.3, below the student’s initial level, with no recovery. The 8B teacher shows the same pattern. At the same time, the optimized alignment metric keeps improving: projected cosine similarity rises from 0.97 to 0.98 with the 4B teacher and from 0.95 to 0.98 with the 8B teacher, even as behavior deteriorates by roughly 35 points. The paper also reports that the untrained student and the 4B teacher already have mid-layer self-CKA around 0.99 despite a large capability gap on MATH-500, which further weakens the case for taking high similarity at face value. Diagnostics show that the main representational changes are concentrated in later student layers, that teacher and student have different layerwise answer-readout patterns under J-Lens, and that neither masking dominant dimensions nor remapping layers by CKA prevents collapse. On the method side, LastOPD avoids the late collapse and improves final MATH-500 over token-only OPD by 5.55 and 4.02 points in the two cross-size Qwen3 settings, while also outperforming continued joint supervision.ad:T431,Read it in three passes: phenomenon, diagnosis, remedy. Start with Figure 1. It already contains the core story: early gain followed by collapse, alignment improving while behavior worsens, and mismatched layerwise readout patterns between teacher and student. Then read the analysis section to see why simple explanations do not hold up: the issue is not just insufficient training, and it is not fixed by a better layer mapping. After that, read the LastOPD method section with one question in mind: why align only the pre-head last layer, and why anneal the latent term away after just 10 steps? Finally, inspect the main results and ablations to separate the effect of alignment location from the effect of temporal crossfading. A solid skim takes about 30 minutes. The most interesting follow-ups are whether the useful latent-supervision window depends on teacher–student gap or task type, whether interpretability tools can predict which layers are safe to distill, and whether the same short-lived auxiliary-loss strategy transfers to multi-objective pretraining.ae:T734,The paper builds on OPD and OPSD. In standard OPD, the student samples on-policy trajectories and an external teacher provides next-token logits at each generated prefix. The student is trained by matching these dense token-level targets. OPSD removes the external teacher by using a second copy of the same initial checkpoint as a privileged teacher. The teacher sees the problem, the ground-truth solution, and the student-generated prefix; the student only sees the problem. This transfers gold-conditioned local guidance to the student.

The limitation is that prior OPSD keeps the teacher frozen. The authors probe fixed incorrect trajectories and show that a frozen gold-conditioned teacher often prefers EOS at incorrect endpoints rather than tokens that initiate reflection or correction. Meanwhile, the student’s tendency to reflect increases during training, making the frozen teacher less suitable for later on-policy prefixes.

Dynamic Co-Evolution addresses this by updating the privileged teacher across rounds. After each training update, the resulting checkpoint initializes both the next student and a detached gold-conditioned teacher. The teacher is still frozen within a round, which preserves a stable target, but it is refreshed between rounds so that revision behaviors learned by the student can become part of the next round’s supervision. This is more adaptive than a permanently frozen teacher and more stable than a fully online teacher.

Self-Refined Concise Learning addresses the cost side of stronger revision. More self-checking and backtracking can improve correctness but also inflate output length. SRCL trains on answer-verified, shorter rewrites of the same on-policy responses. DCE improves the ability to recover from mistakes; SRCL encourages the model to keep that ability while using fewer tokens.af:T5fe,The experiments use Qwen3 models at 8B, 4B, and 1.7B scale and evaluate Average@12 on four competition-level math reasoning benchmarks. Compared with OPSD, DCE improves Average@12 by 35.41, 37.15, and 12.98 percentage points at 8B, 4B, and 1.7B respectively. Matched-budget controls indicate that the gains are not explained by longer generations alone.

SRCL is most visible under constrained inference budgets. Under the lowest tested 8K evaluation budget, DCE+SRCL reaches 35.07% Average@12 with a mean of 7,500 output tokens per response. It outperforms the OPSD test-time-scaling control by 6.60 percentage points while generating about 692 fewer tokens per response.

The teacher-behavior probes are central. On fixed incorrect Qwen3-8B trajectories from AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and AIME 2026, the frozen gold-conditioned teacher assigns 94.5% average probability to EOS at incorrect endpoints and only 22.0% to observed reflection cues such as “Wait”. After DCE, the privileged teacher’s endpoint EOS probability drops from 90.4% to 41.3%, while its probability on observed reflection tokens rises from 32.8% to 77.4%. This shows that the local supervision changes direction: from stopping at a wrong endpoint toward checking and revising.

Ablations compare per-round teacher updates with frozen, EMA, and periodic alternatives. Updating the teacher every round performs best, suggesting that teacher refresh frequency is a substantive training variable in reasoning self-distillation rather than an implementation detail.b0:T445,The central concept is strategic diversity: substantive variation in how a problem is approached, not lexical variation or embedding-space distance. The paper proposes two ways to generate strategically diverse self-training data using the model itself. The first adapts Verbalized Sampling: the model lists multiple possible approaches with estimated probabilities, and each approach is then used as a hidden instruction for generating a full response. The second method, Groot, asks the model to build a hierarchical decision tree over approaches and samples distinct root-to-leaf paths. This is natural for competitive programming, where solutions branch by algorithm, data structure, and implementation choices. For story planning, where narrative decisions are interdependent and less hierarchical, the unstructured VS-style approach is more suitable. Compared with high-temperature IID sampling, both methods force the model to commit to different approaches before producing the final answer, so they change the strategy distribution rather than only perturbing token-level realization.b1:T86a,实验主干基于 Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct 与 PMC-VQA。SFT 使用 10k 训练题、1.5k 验证题、2k clean test，且作者检查了训练集与 clean test 在图像内容和 image-question 对上的无重叠。三个 SFT 配置的最佳 checkpoint 都出现在半个 epoch。最关键的 clean-test 结果是：仅语言侧 LoRA 的 M1-L，correct-image accuracy 只提升 +1.10 个百分点，95% paired bootstrap CI 为 -0.85 到 +3.05，统计上并不稳；但 visual-benefit events 减少 2.40 个点，image sensitivity 下降 5.60 个点，同时样本级别上出现 155 个新获得的视觉收益案例和 203 个丢失案例。这说明净准确率几乎不变时，底层决策机制已经明显重排。作者还发现扩大适配范围到 merger 或 vision encoder 并没有带来更好的 held-out 视觉效用，反而 clean-test accuracy 更低，说明在这个数据量和任务设置下，更多视觉参数可训练并不等于更好地学会用视觉。GRPO 部分，标准 answer-only GRPO 在 2000 prompt trajectory 上持续优化，但验证集选出的 M2-500 在 clean test 上几乎不改准确率，说明 reward 在被优化，但收益没有转移到最终任务指标。证据目标部分，M3 与 M4 的差异揭示了一个重要现象：如果用 canonical option token 来计分，得到的是一种“选项支持度”信号；如果沿真实生成 token path 计分，学到的则更接近实际解码行为。作者又做了 500/1000/2000 prompt exposure 的 dose-matched 比较，发现 evidence score 的提升里既有训练暴露量带来的 acquisition，也有从训练集到验证集的 transfer，而且不同 score component 的变化方向并不一致。换句话说，看到 evidence objective 变好，不能直接推断模型更会看图，还要问是哪个 token、哪一段路径、在哪个数据子集上变好。全文的 paired transition 分析是亮点，因为它把 aggregate 指标拆回到单题层面的 gained/lost visual-benefit cases，能看清楚模型是在“把原来依赖图像的题做成了不依赖图像也能答对”，还是“真的学会了更多视觉证据”。b2:T56b,The paper has three technical layers. First, it defines a controlled evaluation protocol with three conditions per question: Correct image (C), NoImage (N), and Shuffled image (S). From these, it derives metrics such as visual-benefit rate (VBR), visual-harm rate (VHR), and image sensitivity (IS), which are more informative than plain accuracy because they test whether the answer depends on the image in the right way. Second, it compares different SFT adaptation scopes on Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct: M1-L applies LoRA only to language-model attention projections; M1-ML also trains the multimodal merger; M1-VML further adapts the vision encoder. This isolates whether opening more of the visual pathway actually improves held-out visual utility. Third, it studies RL-style objectives. Standard answer-only GRPO is initialized from M1-L to form M2. Then two evidence-objective variants are introduced: M3 uses canonical option-token scores, while M4 scores tokens along the actual generation path. This is an important implementation-level distinction. The paper shows that the meaning of the reward changes depending on which token path is scored, and it uses matched-dose comparisons to separate objective effects from simple training exposure effects. A supplementary SLAKE experiment further examines how native-answer token learning interacts with generation and stopping behavior.b3:T6ef,The main experiments use Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct on PMC-VQA, with 10k training questions, 1.5k validation questions, and a 2k clean test set with no image-content or image-question overlap with training. All selected SFT checkpoints occur at half an epoch. The most important result is that M1-L, the language-only LoRA SFT setup, changes correct-image accuracy by only +1.10 percentage points on the clean test, with a 95% paired bootstrap confidence interval of -0.85 to +3.05. Yet visual-benefit events decrease by 2.40 points and image sensitivity drops by 5.60 points. At the paired-example level, the model gains 155 visual-benefit cases but loses 203, showing substantial internal redistribution despite a small net accuracy change. Expanding adaptation to the merger or vision encoder does not help; broader multimodal adaptation lowers clean-test accuracy, suggesting that more trainable visual components do not automatically translate into better visual use under this data regime. For RL, standard answer-only GRPO continues to optimize its reward, but the validation-selected checkpoint M2-500 leaves clean-test accuracy nearly unchanged. The evidence-objective analysis is the most nuanced part: M3 and M4 behave differently because canonical option-token scoring and generation-path-aligned scoring capture different signals. Dose-matched comparisons at 500, 1000, and 2000 prompt exposures show that improvements in evidence scores mix together training-dose effects, score acquisition, and transfer, and that different score components move for different reasons. The paired transition analysis is especially useful because it reveals whether the model is truly learning to use visual evidence or merely becoming correct in a way that is less image-dependent.b4:T522,The proposed method is Calibrated Importance Sampling, or CIS. Standard token-level correction uses the importance weight r = π_train(y_t|h_t) / π_infer(y_t|h_t). The paper argues that this ratio entangles two factors: the confidence of the sampled token and the actual discrepancy between the inference and training engines. It rewrites the ratio as a function of token confidence and an additive log-odds displacement ε_t. If the inference probability of the sampled token is p and the training engine shifts its log-odds by ε, the corrected probability can be written as sigmoid(logit(p)+ε), giving a ratio of roughly exp(ε)/(1-p+p exp(ε)). This shows why a fixed ratio threshold is poorly calibrated: the same ε produces a much larger ratio change for low-confidence tokens than for high-confidence tokens. CIS clips ε directly instead of clipping r. Since the measured ε distribution is approximately invariant across confidence buckets, a single threshold can be applied to the discrepancy component. When mapped back to the ratio, this becomes a confidence-dependent cap that is tighter for high-confidence tokens. The theoretical analysis shows that CIS bounds the second-moment term that can explode under exact importance correction, while introducing a bias controlled by the truncated excess.b5:T5de,RLTL;DR has two components. The first changes rollout collection. Instead of K independent parallel attempts, the agent solves the same task sequentially. After each failed attempt, the verifier is run and exposes error messages, failed assertions, tracebacks, or final-state checks. The same policy then reads the failed attempt and verifier output and writes a short TL;DR insight, such as a reminder to paginate search results. The next attempt is conditioned on the original task plus the accumulated insights. This converts some tasks from a zero-success sampling regime into a regime where at least one successful trajectory can be found.

The second component changes optimization. Sequential exploration alone does not solve test-time performance, because evaluation requires a first-attempt solution without any accumulated insights in context. The paper therefore enables backpropagation through the in-context insight tokens, about 17 tokens per insight. These insights are inserted as user messages, but their tokens receive an SFT-style loss. The policy thus internalizes a mapping from task descriptions to high-level reminders. GRPO can still be applied to rollout action tokens with a clipped objective, using epsilon 0.2, but the ablations show that the insight-token loss is the dominant source of improvement. This distinguishes the method from ordinary reflection prompting: the reflection is not only used at inference or sampling time; it is made into a parameter-learning target.b6:T4f3,The experiments use Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking as the base agent on verifiable agentic and coding tasks. Episodes allow up to 50 actions, and the verifier returns a binary reward together with rich failure observations. The selected tasks are intentionally difficult: the base policy often fails even after 128 attempts. In this regime, standard GRPO stays nearly flat, with Pass@1 around 0% to 1%.

Sequential sampling improves exploration. On tasks where independent attempts do not produce useful successes, conditioning later attempts on self-generated TL;DR insights yields Pass@k in the 14% to 59% range. However, if insights are only used during sampling and not learned into the model, evaluation without insights remains close to the original policy.

With the full RLTL;DR training procedure, evaluation is done without insights and without sequential sampling. The model must solve the task on the first attempt. Pass@1 reaches 11% to 14%, while GRPO remains at 0% to 1%. The strongest ablation disables the GRPO loss and keeps only the SFT loss on insight tokens; this recovers most of the full method’s performance. That result indicates that parameterizing the task-to-insight mapping, rather than reinforcing final rollout tokens, is the central mechanism.b7:T481,Read the Introduction and Methods closely. The Introduction gives the key failure condition for RLVR: the verifier may be correct, but the policy never reaches a successful trajectory, so there is no useful learning signal. In Methods, focus on the separation between rollout action tokens trained by GRPO and self-generated insight tokens trained through an enabled backpropagation mask. Two issues are worth deeper inspection. First, insight quality: the same policy writes the insights, so incorrect or over-specific lessons may be learned. Second, distributional reuse: the method should work best when hard tasks share recurring failure patterns. If each task requires a unique insight, the task-to-insight mapping may generalize less reliably.b8:T8a8,ProVer 的名字对应三步：Propose、Verify、Credit。

第一步 propose：在同一个 GRPO group 内，作者拿成功轨迹和失败轨迹做对比，让一个 agentic judge 去定位成功轨迹中“可能导致结果分叉”的片段。这里的关键设计是只让 judge 负责提出候选 segment，而不是直接给 segment 打 reward。这样做是为了利用 LLM 在模式识别和对比解释上的长处，但避免把训练信号完全交给一个容易漂移、可被利用的评审器。

第二步 verify：对 propose 出来的片段，恢复该片段开始前和结束后的环境状态，从这两个边界状态分别用当前策略采样新的 continuations。作者用两端 continuation 的经验终局成功率之差，来估计这个 segment 的 advantage。直观上，如果“经过这个片段之后”的状态更容易被当前策略继续做成，那么这个片段就确实为成功创造了更好的后续条件；反之，如果差异不明显，说明 judge 提议的片段未必真关键。这个设计很像把局部 credit assignment 建立在可验证 outcome 上，而不是建立在中间过程的语言评价上。

第三步 credit：只有当验证得到的 segment advantage 为正时，才把这部分额外 credit 加到原始 GRPO 的 token-level 更新上，而且只加给该 segment 内的 policy token。也就是说，ProVer 不是替换 GRPO，而是在 GRPO 的轨迹级优势之上叠加一个局部、稀疏、经验证的 bonus。这样既保留了 GRPO 不需要 value model 的优点，也缓解了 uniform advantage 带来的噪声。

和已有路线相比，区别主要有三点。与 critic/value-based 方法相比，它不依赖一个单独学习的中间价值估计器，因此少了一层 distribution shift 和 reward hacking 风险。与 process reward model 或 LLM evaluator 直接打分相比，它不直接信 judge，而是要求 outcome-level verification。与对所有中间状态做 exhaustive branching 相比，它只在被提议的关键片段边界做分支采样，计算成本更低。论文的核心创新不在某个复杂公式，而在这个“proposal by model, verification by environment outcome”的分工。b9:T677,ProVer has three stages: Propose, Verify, and Credit.

In the propose stage, an LLM-based judge compares successful and failed trajectories from the same GRPO group and selects a segment in a successful trajectory that may have caused the divergence in outcome. The judge is used only for localization, not for direct reward assignment. This is an important design choice: it leverages model-based pattern recognition without trusting model judgment as the final training signal.

In the verify stage, the method restores the environment states immediately before and after the proposed segment, then samples fresh continuations from the current policy from both boundary states. The difference in empirical terminal success rates estimates the segment’s advantage. Intuitively, if the post-segment state is much easier for the current policy to complete successfully than the pre-segment state, then the segment likely contributed real causal progress.

In the credit stage, only positively verified segment advantages are added to the original GRPO advantages, and only for policy tokens inside the proposed segment. So ProVer does not replace GRPO. It augments GRPO with sparse, localized, outcome-grounded bonus credit.

Relative to prior approaches, the distinction is clear. It avoids a separately trained value model, so it reduces dependence on critic generalization. It avoids directly optimizing against an LLM evaluator’s intermediate scores, so it is less exposed to evaluator gaming. And it avoids exhaustive branching from every intermediate state, so it is much cheaper than full Monte Carlo credit assignment over the whole trajectory.ba:T50c,The paper introduces DSAR, the Deceptive Safety Alignment Rate, to measure safety inconsistency between the reasoning trace and the final answer within the same generation. The evaluation pipeline uses an LLM judge with detailed instructions. It performs sentence-level safety assessment over the reasoning trace, and also judges the safety of the full reasoning trace and the final answer. This makes it possible to identify cases where the model reasons toward harmful compliance but gives a safe refusal, as well as cases where apparently safe reasoning leads to an unsafe final response. The proposed mitigation is SARA, Safety-Aware Reasoning Alignment, an RL-based method with two objectives. The first objective strengthens reasoning-level safety awareness, meaning the model should explicitly detect harmful intent or unsafe candidate behavior during reasoning. The second objective enforces consistency between the reasoning trace and the final answer, so that safe reasoning is not overridden at the answer stage. Sage provides answer-aware and answer-agnostic modes to cover both curated prover-ready data construction and problem-only formalization.bf:T711,The method is simple, but the framing is sharp. In standard multi-reward GRPO, the total reward is the sum of reward components, and the advantage is computed by centering and dividing by the within-group standard deviation of that total reward. The paper expands this variance term into the sum of all pairwise covariances among reward components. This reveals the issue: covariance mixes two effects, dependence and scale. If one reward has large variance, or if large-scale rewards are strongly positively correlated with others, they can inflate the denominator and shrink the advantage for the whole group.

CorrGRPO keeps the numerator unchanged: it still uses the centered total reward, so the relative weighting of reward components in the objective is preserved. The change is only in the denominator. Instead of covariance-based normalization, it uses Pearson-correlation-based normalization. In effect, each covariance term is divided by the corresponding component standard deviations, removing scale dependence. The diagonal terms of the resulting correlation matrix give equal footing to all reward components with nonzero within-group variance, while off-diagonal terms capture only the strength and direction of dependence. This lets the normalization remain sensitive to whether rewards reinforce or conflict with each other, without letting large numerical scales dominate.

An important practical point is that CorrGRPO does not redefine reward aggregation and does not require a new critic. It only changes advantage scaling, so it can be inserted into existing GRPO pipelines with low implementation cost. It is also conceptually different from manual reward reweighting or simple reward rescaling, because it modifies the normalization statistics rather than the reward objective itself.c0:T526,The experiments cover three naturally multi-reward domains: code generation, tool calling, and agent security, using models from 0.5B to 8B parameters. The paper compares CorrGRPO against standard GRPO and related variants, and reports improvements in code accuracy and training efficiency, tool-call accuracy, and the utility–security tradeoff for agents. It also claims an expansion of the empirical Pareto frontier between competing reward objectives.

The most important empirical story is not a single benchmark number. First, in heterogeneous-reward settings, CorrGRPO is more robust because small-scale rewards are no longer drowned out by the covariance structure of large-scale rewards. Second, in tradeoff-heavy settings such as agent security, correlation-based normalization better preserves the distinction between conflicting rewards, which improves the balance between task utility and safety. Third, in code and tool-use tasks where rewards are partly positively correlated, standard GRPO can over-shrink updates when large-scale rewards dominate the denominator, while CorrGRPO avoids that failure mode. 具体实现有几个关键点。第一，retriever 只在 query side 做 LoRA 适配，而不是全量更新双塔或 cross-encoder，这样把内存和训练开销压到可控范围。第二，retriever 的训练信号不是单一来源，而是两部分结合：一部分是 retrieval turn 上的 trajectory-level RL credit，也就是把最终可验证 reward 反传到检索动作对应的查询表示；另一部分是 RAG likelihood term，用来衡量当前检索到的证据是否支持目标答案。前者解决“检索是否帮助任务成功”，后者解决“检索内容是否语义上支持答案”，两者结合比纯 outcome reward 更稳定。第三，作者没有采用经典 bilevel 的二阶近似、unrolling 或 implicit differentiation，因为这些方法在大模型+检索器联合训练时计算和显存都太重；也没有采用需要维护 original / perturbed 两个 lower-level state 的 first-order estimator，因为 retriever adaptation 下这会带来明显的额外显存。BRIDGE 的做法是利用 landscape analysis 说明 lower-level optimal value 对 θ 并不近似常数，因此不能直接套用更激进的简化；随后借助一种单状态的一阶近似来估计上层梯度，在不维护第二个 lower-level model 的前提下保留较好的梯度方向。

从机制上看，这个方法和普通 joint training 的区别在于：joint training 默认 retriever 与 policy 对称共适应，而 BRIDGE 强调非对称依赖，retriever 更新是为 policy 构造更好的信息条件，policy 更新则是在该条件下学习行为。作者的论点是，在多跳 QA 这类任务里，如果证据链条没先暴露出来，policy 学不到正确推理；因此把两者放在同一层级同时学，容易让 policy 过早吸收错误信用。c4:T834,BRIDGE is a first-order bilevel optimization framework for retrieval-augmented agentic RL. The upper-level variables are the LLM policy parameters θ, and the lower-level variables are the retriever parameters η. The goal is not simple alternating optimization. Instead, the lower level seeks a retriever that best supports the current policy’s answer generation, and the upper level then updates the policy using rollouts produced with that retriever.

Several implementation choices are central. First, the retriever is adapted only through a query-side LoRA module, rather than full retriever finetuning. This keeps memory and compute manageable. Second, retriever learning combines two signals: trajectory-level RL credit at retrieval turns, and a RAG-style likelihood term that scores whether retrieved evidence supports the target answer. The RL signal captures whether retrieval helped the task succeed, while the likelihood term stabilizes training by rewarding semantic support for the answer. Third, the method avoids classical bilevel solvers based on unrolling, conjugate gradient, or implicit differentiation, because these are too expensive in the large-model setting. It also avoids first-order estimators that maintain two lower-level states for the original and perturbed problems, since that is memory-heavy for retriever adaptation. The authors show that a common simplification—treating the lower-level optimal value as nearly constant with respect to θ—does not hold here. Guided by a landscape analysis, BRIDGE uses a single-state first-order approximation that preserves useful gradient direction while removing the need for a second lower-level model.

The key distinction from standard joint training is asymmetry. Joint training treats retriever and policy as co-equal components that adapt together. BRIDGE treats retrieval as an upstream condition for policy learning. In multi-hop QA, if the evidence chain is not exposed first, the policy cannot learn the right reasoning behavior. The bilevel structure is meant to preserve that dependency during co-adaptation.c5:T628,The evaluation covers 7 open-domain QA benchmarks and 5 medical QA benchmarks, with 3B and 7B backbones. The headline result is that on the open-domain suite, BRIDGE improves average exact match over the strongest baseline, VT-Search, by 7.1 points for the 3B model and 2.3 points for the 7B model. On the medical benchmarks, it achieves the best average answer accuracy and reasoning quality. The larger gain at 3B is consistent with the paper’s premise: smaller models benefit more when the retrieval bottleneck is fixed upstream.

The supporting analyses are important. First, order-sensitivity experiments show that adapting the retriever before optimizing the policy yields larger reward gains than the reverse order, directly supporting the hierarchical dependency claim. Second, BRIDGE reduces peak memory per retriever update by 49.7% relative to a two-state first-order estimator, while keeping its gradient estimate closely aligned with that estimator. This suggests the efficiency gain is not coming from an overly crude approximation. Third, the landscape analysis shows that the lower-level optimal value changes noticeably with policy parameters, which invalidates a stronger constant-value approximation used in some prior bilevel methods. Fourth, ablations indicate that both retrieval-turn RL credit and the RAG likelihood term matter; removing either weakens performance. Even without every benchmark number in the provided text, the experimental story is coherent: the gains come from better credit assignment, not from adding more generic training steps.c6:T83a,The method has two stages: diagnosis and training-time credit gating.

The diagnostic tool is a fixed-rollout counterfactual test. Instead of resampling a new response under a modified image, the method teacher-forces the exact same generated response under both the original image I and an intervened image I^cf. This removes confounding from trajectory changes. Evidence-Function Sensitivity (EFS) measures how much the predictive distribution at claim tokens changes under the intervention. If the model is visually responsive, EFS should increase. But EFS alone is not enough, because changing the image can shift the likelihood of the whole response. To isolate claim-level support, the paper defines claim persistence and calibrates it using residual tokens from the same rollout, so that trajectory-wide likelihood drift is discounted. This separation between sensitivity and retractability is the conceptual core of the paper.

Based on that diagnosis, the authors propose Persistence-Aware Credit Gating (PACG). During RL training, they identify routed direct visual claims, meaning token spans that are treated as direct image-grounded assertions. For tokens with positive advantage, claims that retract sufficiently under the counterfactual keep their full positive credit, while unusually persistent claims receive attenuated positive credit. Negative-advantage tokens and non-routed tokens are left unchanged. The design is intentionally conservative: it does not punish all visual tokens, and it does not require supervised labels for claim support. It only reduces positive reinforcement where the model appears to preserve unsupported visual assertions. PACG is designed to plug into existing RLVR optimizers such as DAPO and VPPO, and it adds no inference-time cost.

Compared with prior perception rewards, token reweighting, or multimodal process reward models, the novelty here is the target of supervision. The paper is less concerned with whether the model looked at the image, and more concerned with whether the specific visual statement should survive when the evidence is removed.c7:T664,The paper begins with a strong empirical observation.
