This shows that the issue is not rare noise; outcome-level RL can systematically reinforce unsupported claims.

The diagnostic experiments reveal what the authors call Sensitivity–Persistence Decoupling. Under DAPO and VPPO, training increases EFS and improves overall retractability, yet unsupported claims become more persistent. GRPO also increases EFS, but without the same deterioration in unsupported-claim persistence. This is an important result because it ties the problem to the optimizer and its credit-broadcasting behavior, rather than treating it as an unavoidable property of multimodal RL.

在损失设计上，作者没有对整条混合轨迹统一套一个 KL，而是按 token 来源拆开。对学生自己提出的 token 位置，用 reverse KL，让学生在自己访问到的状态上向教师分布靠拢，但不过度覆盖教师所有 mode；这更接近 on-policy distillation 的目标，也更适合小模型在自身可实现的解空间里收缩分布。对教师接管时生成的 token 位置，用 forward KL，让学生直接模仿教师纠偏后的 continuation；这部分更像局部离线蒸馏。这个 source-split objective 是论文最有方法含量的地方，因为它把 on-policy 和 off-policy 蒸馏拼接在同一条轨迹里，而不是简单做数据级混合。

工程上，作者还实现了 fused inference engine，把 teacher 和 student 共置于一个 serving instance，分别维护 KV cache，并根据当前 proposer/verifier 角色调度请求。这个系统细节不是论文主创新，但它解决了双模型交替 rollout 的实际开销问题，否则 IPD 很容易因为 teacher intervention 过于频繁而失去训练效率。

和已有 OPD 的区别主要有三点。第一，传统 OPD 默认学生轨迹始终可被教师稳定评估，IPD 明确承认并处理 unanchoring。第二，已有方法常在样本级混合 on-policy/off-policy 数据，IPD 在 token 级别区分 supervision。第三，教师不是静态 labeler，而是交互式纠偏者。这个设计更像 DAgger 在语言模型蒸馏场景下的细化版本，但作者把它落到了 token-level KL 训练上，而不是只做行为克隆。cb:T952,The core method is Interactive-Policy Distillation, or IPD. Instead of letting the student generate a full trajectory and querying the teacher afterward, or letting the teacher dominate the whole rollout, IPD uses a bidirectional propose-and-verify state machine. Student and teacher alternate between proposer and verifier roles. The current proposer emits tokens, and the verifier checks whether the trajectory remains within an acceptable region. If the student starts to drift, the teacher takes over and provides a corrective continuation. Once the trajectory returns to a region the student can plausibly continue from, control is handed back to the student. The resulting training sample is therefore a mixed-source trajectory, with some tokens proposed by the student and others by the teacher.

The loss is the most interesting part. Rather than applying one KL objective to the entire mixed trajectory, the paper splits supervision by token source. On student-generated positions, it uses reverse KL, which is more aligned with on-policy distillation: the student is trained on states it actually visits and is encouraged to concentrate on realizable modes instead of covering every teacher mode. On teacher-generated positions, it uses forward KL, effectively imitating the teacher’s corrective continuation. This source-split objective is the main methodological contribution because it combines on-policy and off-policy distillation within the same trajectory at token granularity, not just by mixing datasets.

The paper also includes a fused inference engine that co-hosts teacher and student in one serving instance, keeps separate KV caches, and schedules requests according to the current proposer/verifier roles. This is not the conceptual core, but it matters in practice because frequent teacher intervention would otherwise make rollout expensive.

Relative to prior OPD work, the differences are clear. Standard OPD assumes teacher supervision remains meaningful on student rollouts; IPD explicitly handles the case where that assumption breaks. Prior methods often mix on-policy and off-policy data at the sample level; IPD distinguishes them at the token level. And the teacher is not just a static labeler, but an interactive corrector. The overall flavor is reminiscent of DAgger-style correction, but adapted to token-level KL training for language models.cc:T683,The experiments focus on mathematical reasoning distillation across four teacher-student pairs. The main metrics are benchmark-averaged mean@8 and best@8 accuracy. The headline result is that IPD achieves the best average performance and leads on most individual benchmarks. The most concrete number given in the paper summary is on Qwen3-30B-A3B to Qwen3-1.7B-Base distillation: IPD surpasses the mean@8 of OPD trained for a full epoch, 279 steps, after only 60 training steps. That is a strong data-efficiency result.

The experimental story appears to support three claims. First, the gain is not merely from adding more teacher tokens, but from intervening when the student drifts, re-anchoring the trajectory, and then returning control. Second, the source-split objective matters because student-origin and teacher-origin tokens play different roles and should not share one uniform divergence. Third, the method is reasonably robust across training datasets rather than tied to one specific reasoning corpus.

The provided full-text excerpt does not include all tables, but the paper likely contains ablations along the following lines: teacher intervention without source-split loss, source-split loss without interactive takeover, different intervention frequencies or acceptance criteria, and comparisons against pure SFT, pure OPD, and possibly RLVR-style baselines. Those ablations are important because IPD introduces multiple moving parts, and the main question is which component contributes most.

Overall, the empirical contribution is best understood as making OPD more stable and sample-efficient, not as replacing the distillation paradigm itself.cd:T594,A good skim path is: problem definition, state machine, loss, then efficiency results. Start with the Introduction to understand teacher unanchoring and why naive OPD can fail for strong-teacher and weak-student pairs. Then read the methodology figure for the bidirectional propose-and-verify process and make sure it is clear when the teacher takes over and when the student resumes. Next, focus on the source-split objective and the rationale for reverse KL on student tokens versus forward KL on teacher tokens. Finally, inspect the main benchmark table and the training-step comparison curves to see whether the method really improves data efficiency over OPD.

For a skim, 20 to 30 minutes should be enough. Prioritize the method diagram, the main result table, the step-efficiency plots, and the ablation table. For deeper reading, check how the acceptance region is defined, whether it depends on heuristic thresholds, how often teacher intervention happens in practice, and how much throughput the fused engine actually recovers. Those details determine whether the method is suitable for large-scale post-training pipelines.

A longer-term question worth keeping in mind is whether IPD is only useful for small-model reasoning distillation or whether the same framework could be adapted to online teacher shaping earlier in the training stack. The paper does not fully answer that, but it provides a plausible template.ce:T455,ABC, or Advantage-Based Control Variates, reformulates trajectory-level control variates using learned advantage and value functions. Standard PPO often relies on TD-style advantage estimates, where value approximation error can bias the update. GRPO removes the learned critic and instead normalizes returns within groups of rollouts. ABC takes a different route: it inserts learned advantage and value terms as control variates for the policy-gradient estimator while preserving unbiasedness. The paper characterizes the covariance of this estimator and relates it to the return decomposition used in Direct Advantage Estimation. It then combines ABC with DAE into an actor-critic algorithm. The critic is first trained on offline data to approximate the advantage and value functions of the target policy, and actor and critic are then updated with online sampled trajectories. The theory shows that the true advantage and value functions minimize the covariance; in deterministic environments, the excess variance can be bounded by return prediction error from the estimated advantage-value decomposition.cf:T40a,The paper first compares two forward passes of the same policy over the same sampled response: one with the normal context and one augmented with a hindsight skill written after the trajectory. The skill makes the policy a better actor, but produces little change in next-token distributions. It instead changes hidden states across many response tokens. PR-OPD uses this observation directly. After a GRPO warm start, the policy continues on-policy RL. For each completed trajectory, the model writes a hindsight skill, then re-reads its own sampled response with that skill as a stop-gradient privileged teacher. The student processes the same response without the skill. Instead of matching teacher logits, the student hidden states are passed through lightweight per-layer MLP projectors and aligned to the teacher hidden states across layers. The policy, hindsight analyzer, and teacher share the same weights; the only added module is the projector, and there is no extra teacher model, skill library, or inference-time context.d0:T4bf,REVO is an off-policy distillation framework that performs multiple learner updates per student rollout. The base objective is token-level reverse KL between the student and teacher next-token distributions at student-generated prefixes. Naive reuse has two mismatches. Prefix mismatch comes from using prefixes generated by an older student; REVO handles it with geometrically normalized and capped prefix weights to avoid high-variance products of likelihood ratios over long prefixes. Current-token mismatch comes from keeping tokens sampled by an older student; REVO replaces them with one-step resampling from the current student at the stored prefix, avoiding full trajectory regeneration. The second component is variance-guided token prioritization. REVO estimates the variance of the student-teacher log-probability ratio and uses it as a bounded weight for token-level updates. Under a local realizability condition, this variance equals the inner product between the ordinary gradient and the natural gradient of the local reverse-KL objective, linking it to local natural-gradient progress. Empirical diagnostics further connect it to the signal-to-noise ratio of finite-sample logit-gradient estimates.d1:T748,The method has two layers. The first is CaRE-Divergence, a token-level objective that interpolates between Forward KL and Reverse KL based on relative confidence. Confidence is measured by normalized entropy from a single forward pass: sharper distributions imply higher confidence. When the teacher is more confident than the student, the gate moves toward Forward KL, encouraging support coverage. When the teacher is less confident, the gate moves toward Reverse KL, making the update more mode-seeking and less sensitive to the teacher’s unreliable tail. The paper considers both hard and sigmoid-based soft gates, but the key idea is that the gate depends on the teacher-student confidence gap rather than a fixed global coefficient.

The second component is Revival, a sequence-level rejection rule. The authors argue that single-pass entropy only captures aleatoric uncertainty and cannot separate intrinsic ambiguity from hallucination-like epistemic uncertainty. To address this, they estimate BALD scores for both teacher and student using Monte Carlo dropout, then reject a distillation update when the teacher is epistemically less reliable than the student. The threshold is defined by running quantiles rather than a fixed scalar, which makes the rule robust to training-time drift in BALD magnitudes.

What distinguishes the paper from prior work is the combination of token-level geometry adaptation and sequence-level supervision rejection. Earlier methods mostly use a static divergence with a global precision-recall bias, or perform filtering at the dataset level. The gradient analysis is also important: the authors argue that no single static divergence can reproduce the conditional behavior of their objective, because a fixed geometry cannot be mean-seeking on some tokens and mode-seeking on others within the same training trajectory.d2:T516,The evaluation spans 8 teacher-student pairs and 11 benchmarks covering instruction following, chat alignment, code generation, math reasoning, and factuality. An important result is that Revival is not tied to CaRE-Divergence alone; when added to Forward KL, Reverse KL, alpha-beta divergence, and Skewed RKL, it consistently improves performance. That suggests the sequence-level rejection mechanism is a fairly general enhancement.

The more informative evidence is in the analysis. The point is not simply that weak teachers hurt; it is that the student is often already better calibrated in those regions and still gets dragged toward unreliable supervision. In standard policy-gradient estimation, the coefficient multiplying each sample’s score-function term is approximately the product of the importance-sampling ratio r and the advantage A. PPO clips only r within a trust region, but if A is large, the effective coefficient rA can still be large and noisy. ACPO clips this product directly to the interval [-alpha, alpha], thereby controlling the actual scalar that scales each sample’s policy-gradient contribution. This has two immediate consequences: both large positive and large negative advantages are constrained in a unified way, and the clipping target is better aligned with the true update magnitude. The paper also shows that ACPO can be plugged into PPO- and GRPO-style pipelines without redesigning the whole training loop. The theory has two parts. First, under explicit assumptions, the second moment of the ACPO gradient estimator is no larger than that of PPO; with an additional assumption, this yields a variance-reduction guarantee. The point is not a strong optimality theorem, but a formal explanation of why clipping rA should be more stable than clipping r alone. Second, the authors connect ACPO to policy mirror descent by interpreting it as the policy-optimization analogue of gradient clipping, and they derive convergence guarantees for gradient-clipped PMD in standard RL settings. Relative to prior work, the novelty is not in a new critic, reward shaping, or rollout scheme, but in changing the clipping target from the IS ratio to the quantity that actually controls update magnitude.d8:T475,The experiments use Qwen2.5-Math-7B and Qwen3 models at 1.7B, 4B, and 8B scales, evaluated on four mathematical reasoning benchmarks with eight matched comparisons. The paper first formalizes an energy-bias view of reconstruction-based extraction. If activations decompose into multiple concept components, the marginal gain from improving reconstruction of component j scales with its energy. As a result, high-dispersion background concepts are favored over low-dispersion forget concepts. This is not presented as a full impossibility theorem, but as a useful incentive-level explanation for why standard extractors blend precise targets into broader features.

SCALPEL modifies the SAE objective with contrastive learning centered on forget anchors. Each forget example is augmented into paraphrases and rewritten variants, and different views of the same anchor are treated as positives. Negatives are sampled from retain data rather than from other forget examples. That design matters: using retain negatives helps separate target-specific structure from shared linguistic and task background, while avoiding the mistake of pushing related forget examples away from each other. After training, the SAE yields a fixed set of sparse forget-associated features. At inference time, the same feature set is available for every input, but each feature is subtracted only when activated by the encoder, producing an explicit and input-dependent internal filter.

Two details are especially important. First, the paper uses a norm-aware feature selection rule, because intervention strength depends both on encoder activation and on the magnitude of the decoder direction. Second, the theory section gives three supporting arguments: reconstruction induces energy bias, contrastive training favors target-selective sparse features, and high-scoring features admit a bound on expected background perturbation. These are best read as justification for the design, not as deletion guarantees.e0:T648,Experiments are run in the controlled TOFU author-level unlearning setting across three model families. The paper compares SCALPEL against mechanistic baselines such as PCA, NMF, and standard SAEs, as well as optimization-based unlearning methods. The evaluation is multi-axis: forgetting effectiveness, retain preservation, feature selectivity, and robustness of the removed trace.

The main empirical picture is consistent. First, at the representation-extraction level, SCALPEL learns features that are more concentrated on the forget target and less entangled with retain-side background structure than reconstruction-only methods. The paper supports this with activation analyses and feature-level diagnostics, including residual-stream studies on Qwen. Second, as an unlearning intervention, SCALPEL achieves competitive forgetting relative to optimization-based baselines while causing less collateral damage on retained knowledge. Third, the norm-aware feature ranking improves over activation-only ranking, confirming that decoder magnitude matters for practical intervention quality. Fourth, ablations show that the contrastive setup is sensitive to positive/negative construction: treating other forget examples as negatives hurts selectivity because it breaks shared target structure.

The evidence is strongest in the controlled benchmark setting. The authors are explicit that this is not certified deletion and not a full solution to GDPR-style erasure. They start from 21 hand-written neutral prompts in single languages and define the objective around the target language probability at the first generated token. They then introduce LIHA, a head-level attribution score computed via activation patching between a clean target-language prompt and a corrupted foil-language prompt. This identifies attention heads whose activations causally push the model toward the correct response language.

Next, they run Edge Attribution Patching over source-head to destination-layer edges. EAP uses a first-order Taylor approximation to estimate the effect of replacing an upstream clean activation with its corrupted counterpart, allowing many edges to be scored with one backward pass per sample. Because this is only an approximation, they cap the candidate set at 2,000 edges per model and then run exact activation patching on each candidate edge. Only edges with sign agreement between EAP and exact patching are retained. The surviving edges are assembled into a DAG, interpreted as the verified first-token broadcasting circuit. Finally, they validate the graph with boundary ablations: removing in-graph edges should hurt language identification, while removing out-of-graph edges should not.

The structural findings are more interesting than the raw scores. Four standalone models show a recurring deep-layer hub topology, where a small number of late heads appear to broadcast language identity forward. The Pythia models also show more explicit multi-hop routing chains. By contrast, Qwen2.5-1.5B Base and Instruct fail the same necessity/irrelevance separation and also have the weakest EAP-to-exact correlation. The authors interpret this conservatively as a pipeline-reliability issue rather than evidence that Qwen lacks such circuits.e3:T505,The study covers six models from four families, roughly 560M to 2.8B parameters: GPT-2, BLOOM-560M, Pythia-1B, Pythia-2.8B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B Base/Instruct. The edge search space grows with model size, from 792 scored edges in GPT-2 to 15,872 in Pythia-2.8B. For tractability, every model is truncated to a 2,000-edge candidate pool before exact verification. After sign-consistent exact patching, final graph sizes range from 816 edges for GPT-2 to 1,016 for Qwen2.5-1.5B.

The most important empirical result is not task performance but validation quality. The paper reports EAP-to-exact-patching correlations as a sanity check on the attribution stage. The four standalone models show stronger agreement and cleaner boundary-ablation behavior, which makes their extracted graphs more credible as functional circuits. The Qwen pair shows weaker correlation and weaker necessity/irrelevance separation, so those graphs should be treated with caution. Another useful aspect is that the analysis goes beyond listing important heads: it verifies head-to-layer edges, which is closer to a causal routing account.

That said, the dataset is tiny, only 21 prompts, so the claims should be read as a careful case study rather than a broad statistical statement about multilingual pretraining.e4:T597,The framework is built on finite structural causal models. The evaluator has access to the full state ξ=(X,H), while the learner may not observe the latent context H. For a query z=(ξ,a), the evaluator defines a structural index σ_M(ξ,a), which records the active context class, the directly affected variable, the value class, and the first structural response delay. A mechanism memory μ is a finite set of tuples θ=(a,c,y,v,δ), and the answer map T_μ(z) is evaluated against the ground-truth mechanism map. The exact mechanism risk R_Q measures full answer equivalence under a fixed probe distribution Q; coordinate risks decompose errors over context, target, value, and delay, while missed and spurious mechanism risks give operational diagnostics. The main theoretical result expresses optimal probe error as a Bayes decision risk and shows that zero error is possible exactly when each learning-interface fiber lies inside a single probe-answer fiber. The adaptation setup introduces a schema map φ from source to target memory, stable and shifted index sets, and losses L_stab and L_shift. Pure transfer fails on shifted mechanisms, while broad relearning can corrupt stable ones. The proposed Causal Core mechanism uses evidence-gated writing and filtered readout, with gates estimated from paired action/reference interventions or propensity-corrected observational data under standard identification conditions.e5:T490,The model abstraction starts with an unobserved physical state x, an observation o=h(x), a fixed language instruction, and an internal representation λ(x) produced by the VLA backbone. A stochastic policy π then generates a continuous-time open-loop action chunk u(t), which is treated as the control input to a nonlinear control-affine dynamical system. Quantities of interest are defined along the controlled trajectory rather than as static labels. For probing, the work constructs an ideal representation in which multiple physical quantities and their propagated values under candidate action trajectories admit shared linear readouts. For steering, it introduces a path-signature-based exponential-family policy. Path signatures summarize continuous action paths through iterated-integral features, and the exponential-family geometry yields a dually flat statistical manifold. This provides a formal link between linear probes in representation space and linear steering of action-trajectory distributions. The key difference from standard LLM LRH is that the represented direction is tied to future dynamics and policy geometry, not only to a static concept.e6:T428,The authors define a growing heterogeneous manifold-mixture model where the number of components, weights, reach, separation, and perturbation scales may change with sample size. Each component can have its own intrinsic dimension and smoothness. They first prove an aggregate minimax lower bound, denoted R_n, which accounts for each component’s difficulty through dimension, smoothness, and effective sample size. They then construct an oracle tangent local-polynomial estimator: it estimates local charts and tangent coordinates, and performs reduced-dimensional polynomial regression in those coordinates. The oracle supplies dimension, smoothness, and bandwidth, but not the tangent projector or the task function. A structure-informed transformer is then built using softmax attention and ReLU feed-forward networks to implement geometric preconditioning, chartwise selection, and local reduced regression in one forward pass. The final analysis separates near-ERM risk into in-context error, approximation error, finite-task error, and optimization error.e7:Ta15,技术方案的关键是实验控制做得很严。作者设定攻击者只能控制一次 tool result 的字节内容，不能改系统提示、用户任务、工具 schema 或服务配置；防守方唯一能控制的是 tokenizer 如何把这些字节映射成 token id。围绕这一点，论文构造了几组条件。

第一组是 Reserved：在注入的 tool 输出里伪造 chat template marker，并让这些 marker 以模型原生的 reserved token id 进入上下文。第二组是 Split：字节完全相同，解码后日志里看到的字符串也完全相同，但通过 tokenizer 设置把这些 marker 编成普通 subword 序列，而不是 reserved id。这样就把“同样文本、不同 token id”直接对比出来。第三组是 Matched：因为 Split 往往会比 Reserved 多出 7 到 33 个 token，单纯多 token 也可能改变行为，所以作者在普通文本别处人为加入同样数量的额外 token，同时保留 marker 的 reserved id。这样 Split 与 Matched 在字节和 token 数上匹配，只差 marker 是否保留 reserved representation。作者把 Split 与 Matched 的攻击成功率差定义为 identity gap，用来估计 reserved representation 本身值多少钱。

这个设计比已有工作更强的地方在于，它不是把 marker 改写成别的文本，也不是把特殊 token 粗暴拆成单字符，而是在字节固定的前提下只改 token id。这样可以真正回答“权威来自文本还是来自表示”。

论文进一步往前走了一步，不只停留在现象层面。作者分析了 embedding 层，发现 marker 的 subword embedding 平均值不能替代 reserved token 的向量；但在 Llama-3.1 上，embedding 空间里某个最近邻普通 token 的向量却能近似替代它。基于这一点，作者还构造了 adaptive attacker：搜索非保留 token 里哪些 token 向量最接近 reserved marker，结果确实能找到替代性很强的普通 token。这说明攻击权威并不神秘，它相当程度上压缩在一个学习到的输入向量里，而不是来自复杂的高层模板解析。

另一个重要分析是 base 与 instruction-tuned 配对比较。作者在每个 base / instruct 对上都观察到，instruction-tuned 版本对 reserved marker 的偏好更强。这说明后训练阶段反复在真实对话边界上看到这些控制 token，会把“这是高权限边界”的语义进一步写进表示里。这个结论对 chat model 的训练 recipe 很关键，因为它把安全问题直接连到了 post-training 数据分布和模板设计。e8:T95e,实验主要在 InjecAgent 和 AgentDojo 上做。攻击成功定义为：模型下一次生成里调用了攻击者指定的工具。InjecAgent 覆盖 direct harm 和 data stealing 两类 case；AgentDojo 用来验证多轮 agent loop 下结论是否仍成立。所有配置在温度 0 下重复 3 到 5 次，以减小 serving engine 非确定性带来的偶然波动。

最关键的结果是 fixed-bytes 对比。对 Llama-3.1、GLM-4.5 和 Seed-OSS-36B，把伪造 marker 从 reserved id 改成普通 subword 后，InjecAgent 上的攻击成功率下降 39 到 66 个百分点，而且这个差距在 AgentDojo 的多轮环境里依然存在。也就是说，攻击的大头不是“看起来像模板”，而是“模型真的收到了保留 token”。Qwen3-8B 是一个重要例外：在这个模型上，marker 文本本身已经足够强，reserved 与 split 的差异很小。作者解释说，这不是 reserved representation 不重要，而是原始 readout 已经接近 100%，出现了天花板效应；此前 Deng 等人的单字符拆分实验之所以得到 100.00% 到 99.99% 的近零差异，主要就是因为测量点已经饱和。

Matched 控制实验也很关键。结果显示，额外 token 数本身带来的攻击代价接近 0，因此 Reserved 与 Split 的差异几乎都可以归因于 reserved representation，而不是长度变化或异常分词扰动。这一点把机制解释钉得很牢。

向量层面的实验给出更细的证据。作者发现 subword 平均向量不能复现 reserved marker 的效果，说明简单的“文本组合语义”解释不够；但最近邻普通 token 可以在某些模型上近似替代，说明攻击权威在 embedding 空间里是局部可迁移的。再往前，adaptive attacker 搜索到的正是这类邻近 token，证明防守如果只依赖“禁用 special token 重编码”并不稳固。

最后，论文还系统检查了 Hugging Face 上下载量前 400 的 chat 模型 tokenizer 配置，统计到 67 种不同配置，其中 33 种标准 mitigation 只会重编码声明为 special 的 token，却不会处理 tool 协议 token，例如 <tool_response>。作者进一步验证，这个遗漏在 tool channel 上确实会留下同类风险。这部分很有工程含义，因为它说明现有防护不是理论上不完备，而是在主流 serving 栈里就会漏掉一半左右的配置类型。e9:T97e,The technical contribution is a tightly controlled experimental design. The attacker is allowed to control only the bytes of one tool result. They cannot modify the system prompt, user task, tool schema, or serving configuration. The defender controls only the tokenizer call, and therefore the mapping from bytes to token ids. Around this setup, the paper defines three key conditions.

Reserved keeps the forged chat-template markers as native reserved token ids. Split keeps the bytes identical and therefore the rendered text identical, but forces those same marker strings to be encoded as ordinary subwords rather than reserved ids. This is the core fixed-bytes contrast: same bytes, different ids. Because splitting reserved markers also increases token count, the paper adds Matched, which preserves the reserved ids but injects the same number of extra tokens elsewhere in ordinary text. Split and Matched therefore share bytes and token count, differing only in whether the forged markers retain their reserved representation. The attack-success-rate difference between them is defined as the identity gap.

This design is stronger than prior work because it does not rewrite the marker text and does not rely on crude character-level splitting. It changes only token identity while holding the visible string fixed. That directly answers whether the authority comes from text or representation.

The paper then goes beyond behavioral measurement. It analyzes the embedding layer and shows that the average of the marker's subword embeddings does not substitute for the reserved token vector. However, on Llama-3.1, the nearest ordinary token in embedding space can approximate the reserved marker's effect. An adaptive attacker that searches for non-reserved tokens near the reserved marker indeed finds such substitutes. This is an important mechanistic result: a large part of the authority is concentrated in a learned input vector, not in a high-level parser over template syntax.

Another strong component is the base-versus-instruct comparison. Across every tested base/instruction-tuned pair, the instruction-tuned checkpoint shows a stronger preference for the reserved marker. That suggests post-training repeatedly reinforces the semantics of these control tokens as high-authority boundaries. For chat-model training recipes, this is a direct link between formatting conventions and downstream vulnerability.ea:T94e,The main evaluations use InjecAgent and AgentDojo. Attack success is defined as whether the model's next generation contains the attacker-named tool call. InjecAgent covers both direct-harm and data-stealing cases, while AgentDojo checks whether the same effect persists in a multi-turn agent loop. Each configuration is run three to five times at temperature 0 to reduce noise from serving-engine nondeterminism.

The headline result is the fixed-bytes contrast. On Llama-3.1, GLM-4.5, and Seed-OSS-36B, replacing forged reserved markers with ordinary subwords lowers attack success on InjecAgent by 39 to 66 percentage points. The gap remains visible in AgentDojo's multi-turn setting. This means the attack is not driven mainly by 'looking like a template'; it is driven to a large extent by the model actually receiving reserved token ids. Qwen3-8B is the notable exception. There, the marker text itself already carries most of the attack, and the reserved-versus-split gap is small. The paper argues this is largely a ceiling effect because the readout is already near 100%, which also explains why prior character-splitting experiments reported almost no difference.

The Matched control is critical. The cost of extra tokens alone is close to zero, so the Reserved-versus-Split gap is not explained by length or unusual segmentation. That substantially strengthens the causal claim that the reserved representation itself carries the effect.

The embedding experiments add mechanistic evidence. Subword-vector averaging fails to reproduce the reserved marker's authority, so a simple compositional-text explanation is insufficient. But a nearest-neighbor ordinary token can sometimes approximate it, which implies the authority is locally transferable in embedding space. The adaptive-attacker experiment confirms this by finding non-reserved tokens that behave similarly.

Finally, the paper audits tokenizer configurations for the 400 most-downloaded chat models on Hugging Face. Among 67 distinct tokenizer setups, 33 leave tool-protocol tokens such as <tool_response> untouched under the standard mitigation that only re-encodes declared special tokens. The paper then shows the same reserved-token effect exists on that tool channel as well. This is operationally important because it turns a conceptual weakness into a concrete deployment gap in common serving stacks.eb:T624,This is a must-read paper, and it is worth reading in the order of problem decomposition, controls, mechanism, and deployment consequences.

Start with the introduction and Figure 1. The core observation is simple but easy to miss: the exact same string, such as <|im_start|>, can be one reserved token or several ordinary subwords. The request body, logs, and audit trail are identical; only the token ids differ. That framing carries the whole paper.

Next, read the method section carefully, especially the definitions of Reserved, Split, and Matched, and the identity-gap metric. This is the most important part to understand. Many prompt-injection papers do not separate byte content, token count, and token identity cleanly. Here they are disentangled with unusual care.

In the experiments, prioritize three result blocks. First, compare Llama-3.1, GLM-4.5, Seed-OSS-36B, and Qwen3-8B to understand why Qwen is an exception and why that does not invalidate the main claim. Second, inspect the Matched control to verify that extra tokens are not the driver. Third, read the base-versus-instruct comparisons, because they connect the vulnerability directly to post-training.

If time allows, continue to the embedding analysis and adaptive-attacker section. The most interesting question there is whether the authority of a reserved marker behaves like a discrete symbolic privilege or like a dense region in representation space. End with the tokenizer audit, which grounds the mechanism in real deployment practice. A careful read will take around 60 to 90 minutes.ec:T41e,The method builds on prior results showing that the effect of contiguous context tokens on a query token can be absorbed into transformer feedforward weights as a minimal Frobenius-norm update. For a prompt [α, Y, β], where Y is the safety instruction and β is the user query, the paper compares the feedforward input activation without Y, A_clean, and with Y, A_safe. The induced multiplicative map S(Y)=I+Δq(Y) satisfies S(Y)A_clean=A_safe and is called the Safety Operator. Since the update is a rank-1 perturbation of the identity, it has a single principal dilation direction, the safety direction, with strength governed by λ_safe. The Contrastive Safety Loss then pushes λ_safe up on harmful queries and pushes it toward 1 on harmless queries. The suppression weight ρ controls how strongly harmless-query suppression is enforced. The loss is instantiated in four parameterization spaces: continuous embedding optimization, unconstrained discrete GCG-style search, readability-constrained discrete search, and a mixed hybrid suffix setting.ed:T9c6,方法上有三层设计。第一层是监控器构造。作者用 60 个概念构造合成短文本数据，每个概念有 on-topic / off-topic 样本，然后在模型某层残差流上训练线性 probe 作为 concept monitor，并做校准，使未扰动样本上 TPR 接近 100%。这里的 monitor 不是泛化很强的复杂分类器，而是刻意选择了当前 latent monitoring 文献里最常见、最可部署的线性读出器，因此结论针对性很强。

第二层是“自然能力”测量。作者把若干带 monitor verdict 的历史示例放进上下文，让模型在关键回合生成一个被强制指定的目标输出，再比较有无这些 verdict 时关键层激活的变化方向。结果发现，off-the-shelf 模型虽然不会通过 prompt 直接完成逃逸，但它确实会产生一个与 monitored direction 负相关的 activation edit。作者进一步把这个 edit 向量按常数 α 放大并注入前向过程，发现当 α=8 时，monitor 的 TPR 可以从 1.00 降到 0.27。这个实验很关键，因为它说明失败不是“方向没学到”，而是“控制幅度不够”。

第三层是 model organism。作者用 rank-1 LoRA 训练一个专门会根据上下文 verdict 计算并施加 activation edit 的模型。rank-1 这个选择很有信息量：参数容量极小，等于在问“这种逃逸能力是否需要大规模重写模型，还是只需很薄的一层适配器就能唤醒”。结果是后者。训练后的 organism 能在前向传播内部直接完成逃逸，而且能泛化到训练中没见过的 held-out concept monitors。论文还做了机制分析，排除了“记住每个概念一个固定 edit”的简单解释。证据包括：给更多 in-context demonstrations，edit 与 monitor direction 的对齐更强；把 verdict 标签翻转或污染，对齐会下降甚至反向；说明 edit 是由上下文中的反馈在线计算出来的，而不是离线查表。

作者还测试了两个防御方向。其一是 monitor ensembling，希望不同 monitor 的决策边界不易被同时对齐规避；其二是 OOD detection，希望把被编辑后的异常激活识别出来。结果是两者都能约束当前 organism，但都不构成稳固解法，因为攻击者可以把目标从单一 monitor 扩展到 ensemble，或者把 edit 做得更贴近训练分布。论文的态度比较克制：它没有宣称 latent monitoring 无效，而是指出“不能默认模型没有 activation control”。ee:T95d,The method has three main components. First, the monitor construction. The authors build a synthetic dataset over 60 concepts, with short passages that are on-topic or off-topic for each concept, and train calibrated linear probes on hidden activations to serve as concept monitors. This choice is deliberate. The monitor is simple and representative of the most deployable latent-monitoring setup, rather than a highly specialized classifier.

Second, they measure the model’s native tendency to evade. The context contains prior examples annotated with monitor verdicts. On the critical turn, the model is forced to emit a specified target output, and the authors compare hidden states with and without prior verdict feedback. They find that off-the-shelf models already generate an activation edit aligned with the negative monitored direction. The edit is too small to evade on its own, but if the same edit vector is scaled by a constant factor and injected into the forward pass, evasion appears. At alpha = 8, monitor TPR drops from 1.00 to 0.27. This is an important result because it shows the missing ingredient is magnitude, not direction.

Third, they train a model organism using a rank-1 LoRA. The low rank is informative: the question is whether monitor evasion requires a large behavioral rewrite or only a thin adapter that unlocks an existing capability. The answer is the latter. The finetuned model computes and applies the edit within the forward pass, generalizes to held-out concept monitors, and preserves most benchmark performance. The paper also runs mechanistic tests to reject a simple memorization story. If the model had merely stored one edit per training concept, verdict corruption should not systematically reverse the edit. Instead, alignment improves with more in-context demonstrations and degrades or flips when verdict labels are corrupted, indicating that the edit is computed from feedback in context rather than retrieved from a fixed table.

The defense section evaluates monitor ensembling and OOD detection. Both constrain the current organism, but neither looks like a complete solution. Ensembles can themselves become the attack target, and OOD detectors depend on the edited activations remaining visibly off-distribution. The paper’s claim is measured: latent monitoring is not declared useless, but activation control cannot be assumed away.ef:T790,There are four results that matter most. First, the native capability in off-the-shelf models. With prior verdicts in context, the model already shifts its activations in a direction that lowers monitor scores. The raw shift is insufficient for full evasion, but scaling that same edit to alpha = 8 reduces monitor TPR from 100% to 27%. This shows the capability is already partially present.

Second, the LoRA organism. A rank-1 LoRA is enough to make the model evade within the forward pass, without any external manual scaling. On held-out concept monitors, the average TPR falls to 0.04, which suggests the model learned a more general procedure for inferring the monitored direction from verdicts rather than memorizing only the training concepts. Standard benchmark performance stays within 3.4 points of the base model, so the evasion capability does not require a large sacrifice in general competence.

Third, specificity and robustness. The learned edit mainly targets the active monitor, namely the one whose verdicts appear in context, while leaving unrelated concept monitors much less affected. That is a stronger result than simply lowering all probe scores indiscriminately. The paper also reports robustness to monitor retraining, which argues against overfitting to one fixed probe parameterization.

Fourth, the mechanistic ablations. More demonstrations improve alignment between the edit and the monitored direction. Flipping or corrupting verdict labels weakens the alignment and can even reverse it. These experiments are more informative than raw evasion rates because they show the model is actually using verdict information to compute the edit.

A strong aspect of the experimental design is the forced-output critical turn. It removes the confound where the model could merely change wording or avoid the concept at the surface level, making the measured effect a lower bound on latent-monitor vulnerability.f0:T5d4,For a skim, focus on three pieces. First, read the threat model carefully and understand why the critical-turn output is forced. That design choice is central because it isolates activation editing from policy adaptation. Second, look at the native-capability result and the alpha-scaling experiment; they establish that current models already know the direction of evasion. Third, read the mechanistic section, especially the verdict-corruption, demonstration-count, and active-monitor-specificity analyses. Those are the parts that make the paper more than a one-off attack demo.

If time is limited, Introduction, Threat Model and Setup, the main result figures, the mechanistic analysis, and the defense discussion are enough to capture the paper in about 25 to 35 minutes. If reading more deeply, pay attention to monitor training and calibration, where the edit is measured and injected, how held-out concepts are split, and how retrained monitors are evaluated. Those details determine how far the conclusions transfer to realistic agent-monitoring systems.

Two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. One is whether this capability is mostly unlocked by post-training feedback or whether pretraining already provides the necessary activation controllability. The other is how much the attack weakens when verdicts are only implicit through blocked actions rather than explicit binary tags. The paper treats them as information-equivalent, but real systems may not be so clean.f1:T5be,The method extends prior layer-wise surprisal analysis in two important ways. First, it uses the MECO L2 eye-tracking corpus and splits readers by LexTALE vocabulary proficiency into high- and low-proficiency groups, instead of averaging across readers. Second, it introduces Predictive Depth, a summary statistic for how predictive power is distributed across layers. The point is not only to identify the single best layer, but to characterize whether the predictive mass is concentrated in shallower or deeper layers.

Operationally, the authors take several base LLMs, apply Logit Lens to hidden states from each layer, and compute token-level surprisal layer by layer. They then use those surprisal signals to predict two word-level gaze measures: first-pass gaze duration (FPGD), which reflects earlier processing, and total gaze duration (TGD), which includes rereading and later integration. The central claim is not simply that deeper layers are better, but that the preferred depth profile depends on both reader proficiency and the temporal scope of the gaze measure.

The model choice is sensible for the question. They use base rather than instruction-tuned models because the goal is to probe pretraining-induced linguistic representations, not alignment-modified output behavior. The model set spans Gemma 3, Qwen 2.5, OLMo 2, and Llama 3.1 across multiple sizes, which helps test whether the pattern is family-robust rather than tied to one architecture.f2:T5e0,The main findings visible from the full text are fourfold. First, across 12 tested LLMs, lower-vocabulary readers tend to show deeper Predictive Depth for FPGD, meaning that later-layer surprisal better explains their early reading-time behavior. This is consistent with compensatory processing accounts in reading theory, where less proficient readers rely more on broader context. Second, the proficiency gap is much smaller for TGD. Once the measure includes later fixations and rereading, deeper contextual integration appears important for both groups, reducing the between-group contrast. Third, TGD is generally associated with deeper Predictive Depth than FPGD across proficiency groups, which fits the interpretation that the two gaze measures reflect different stages of processing. Fourth, a leave-one-out analysis over texts shows that selecting an internal layer usually gives small but consistent gains over the final layer on unseen texts.

The experimental design is clean in the sense that the same texts, readers, and models are reused while only proficiency grouping and gaze measure vary. The limitations are also clear: the corpus contains only 12 texts of roughly 100–200 words, so external validity is limited; the predictive gains are weak to modest rather than large; and LexTALE captures vocabulary proficiency, not the full space of language ability. The provided full-content excerpt does not include the complete numerical tables, so no exact coefficients are claimed here.f3:T998,任务设置是经典的 arbitrary-token algebraic identity rule induction。输入由若干三元组样例组成，规则只有 ABA 和 ABB 两种，token 本身没有语义，因而可以较好排除语义记忆和 world knowledge 干扰。模型需要根据上下文样例补全最后一个 token。

作者分析的对象是 Yang et al. 先前识别出的三阶段电路：
1. SA heads：把具体 token 抽象成变量角色，例如第 1 位、第 2 位是否相同；
2. SI heads：在变量层面做序列归纳，识别当前 prompt 服从 ABA 还是 ABB；
3. Retrieval heads：把归纳出的变量关系映射回具体 token，输出答案。

方法上主要用了三类机制分析工具。

第一类是 causal mediation analysis。作者在不同 shot 数下，对不同 head 在特定位置做 patching，测量其对正确答案 logit 或准确率的因果贡献。这里有两个对比条件：abstract condition 用来识别 SA 和 SI，token condition 用来识别 Retrieval。然后按 stage 汇总 head 的 CMA 分数，并比较不同 shot 下 top heads 的重合度。

第二类是 topology stability 分析。作者用 rank-biased overlap 比较各 shot 下每个 stage 的 head 排名，想回答“shot 增加后是不是换了一批头在工作”。结果显示不是。大部分 stage 的 top heads 从 1-shot 到 10-shot 基本稳定，变化主要是同一批头的贡献强度上升。

第三类是 activation patching 与 function vector 干预。作者把高 shot prompt 中相关 heads 的激活补丁打到低 shot，甚至 0-shot prompt 中，观察能否直接救回性能。进一步，他们从显著 heads 提取 function vectors，缩放后注入 residual stream，测试它是否能替代 SI 阶段的计算。结果表明，FV 在很大程度上可以替代 induction stage 的输出，但仍依赖下游 Retrieval heads 完整存在，说明它不是凭空生成答案，而是在已有读出通路上提供了中间表示。

方法设计上有几个细节值得注意。其一，作者选的是无语义 arbitrary token 任务，这让“latent symbolic circuit”这个说法更可信，因为模型很难靠语义联想作弊。其二，他们同时看 Gemma 2-2B、Llama 3.1-8B、Qwen 3-4B 三个家族，避免只在单模型上讲机制故事。其三，0-shot 下 SA 无法直接测试，因为没有完整 C 位置可写入，所以作者主要验证 SI 和 Retrieval 是否已可被外部激活。f4:T892,The task is arbitrary-token algebraic identity induction. Prompts contain several three-token examples following either an ABA rule or an ABB rule, and the model must complete the final token of a query example. Because the tokens are arbitrary strings with no semantic content, the setup minimizes contamination from memorized semantics or world knowledge.

The analysis builds on the three-stage circuit identified in earlier work:
1. Symbolic Abstraction (SA) heads map concrete tokens into variable-like roles.
2. Symbolic Induction (SI) heads infer the underlying rule over those abstract roles.
3. Retrieval heads map the inferred relation back to the concrete answer token.

The paper uses three main tools.

First, causal mediation analysis (CMA). At different shot counts, the authors patch activations for specific heads and positions and measure their causal contribution to the model’s output. They use two contrastive conditions: an abstract condition to identify SA and SI heads, and a token condition to identify Retrieval heads.

Second, topology-stability analysis. They rank heads by stage-specific CMA score and compare rankings across shot counts using rank-biased overlap. This tests whether more examples cause the model to recruit different heads or simply strengthen the same ones.

Third, intervention experiments with activation patching and function vectors. The authors transplant activations from high-shot prompts into low-shot or zero-shot prompts, and they also extract function vectors from CMA-significant heads and inject them into the residual stream. This lets them test whether the induction-stage computation can be externally supplied, and whether downstream retrieval circuitry is still required.

A few design choices are especially good. The arbitrary-token task makes the symbolic-circuit interpretation more credible. The study spans three model families—Gemma 2-2B, Llama 3.1-8B, and Qwen 3-4B—rather than telling a single-model story. And the zero-shot analysis is careful: SA cannot be directly tested there because the relevant C positions do not exist, so the paper focuses on whether SI and Retrieval can already be activated downstream.f5:T8ac,The main empirical result is that the circuit appears early and then gets amplified.

Gemma 2-2B provides the clearest transition: accuracy is only 17% at 1-shot, rises to 93% by 4-shot, and reaches 99% by 10-shot. Despite poor 1-shot behavior, CMA already detects the full three-stage circuit. From 1-shot to 10-shot, the dominant change is quantitative growth in head contribution, not a qualitative reorganization of the circuit. In Gemma, some key heads increase their causal contribution by roughly 8x. For example, the main SI head L14H0 grows from 0.9 to 7.4 on ABB, and the top Retrieval head L18H6 grows from 1.3 to 7.0.

Topology is stable across shot counts. In Gemma, the top-5 heads for SI and Retrieval overlap strongly across adjacent shots, with RBO around 0.81–0.94 versus a random baseline of 0.12. SA is somewhat noisier but still shows a persistent core. This supports the interpretation that demonstrations amplify an existing circuit rather than switch the model to a different mechanism.

The intervention results are the strongest evidence. Patching 10-shot activations from SA, SI, and Retrieval into 1-shot prompts raises accuracy to 88%. At 0-shot, SA cannot be tested directly, but patching only SI and Retrieval activations still lifts accuracy from 1% to 56%. That suggests the downstream infrastructure already exists even before any demonstrations are present.

Function-vector experiments push the argument further. A function vector extracted from CMA-significant heads and injected at 0-shot rescues accuracy up to 86%, but performance collapses to 13% when downstream Retrieval heads are ablated. So the function vector does not bypass the whole computation and directly write the answer; it largely substitutes for the SI-stage output while relying on intact Retrieval heads to read it out. The paper also notes that this substitution is more complete for ABB than for ABA, which hints that the two rules are not implemented in exactly the same way.

The same qualitative pattern appears in Llama 3.1-8B and Qwen 3-4B, though the behavioral transition is less dramatic in Llama because its 1-shot performance is already stronger. That is why Gemma serves as the main analysis case.f6:T628,This one is worth a careful skim with attention to figures rather than every patching detail. Start with the task setup and the three-stage circuit definition so that ABA/ABB and the roles of SA, SI, and Retrieval are clear. Then go straight to the main CMA figure showing how signal changes with shot count. The key point to verify is simple: stable topology, stronger signal. After that, read the topology-stability table to confirm that the same heads remain important. Finally, focus on the two intervention sections: high-shot-to-low-shot activation patching, and function-vector injection with Retrieval ablation.

If you only have 30 minutes, read the introduction, the circuit amplification section, the main figures, and the intervention results. If you go deeper, three questions are worth following closely. First, how exactly the abstract and token contrastive conditions isolate different computations. Second, why ABB seems more replaceable by the function vector than ABA. Third, whether this latent-circuit-amplification story can extend beyond clean symbolic tasks to natural-language reasoning, code induction, or other realistic ICL settings.

For pretraining researchers, the most useful takeaway is not any specific head index. It is the broader possibility that pretraining installs reusable induction machinery in the weights, and prompting mainly moves that machinery from low-gain to high-gain operation. That naturally raises a training question: which data mixtures and objectives are most likely to produce such latent, prompt-addressable circuits?f7:T60e,The method has three main components. First, for a fixed trained decoder-only pre-norm transformer, a layer ℓ, and a target position t, the paper defines a loss-to-go from the intermediate hidden state to the terminal prediction loss. Second, it performs a local second-order analysis around low-loss validation trajectories. The key result is that the dominant curvature of this loss-to-go is approximated by a pullback Fisher operator: start with the Fisher geometry of the output distribution over logits, then pull it back through the Jacobian of the downstream computation from layer ℓ to the output. Intuitively, this operator measures how strongly perturbations in a hidden-state direction affect the final predictive distribution. Third, the paper turns this geometry into measurable signals. Its eigenspectrum identifies output-sensitive directions and approximately prediction-null directions in residual space. For causal transformers, the curvature can be decomposed over token fibers, yielding a tokenwise Fisher-Jacobian saliency score κ_{ℓ,s}. This score is supported only on causal ancestors of the target token and is controlled by downstream Jacobian couplings, making it more loss-faithful than raw attention weights. The same geometry is then used to guide matched-budget rank allocation, structured token pruning, and low-rank student distillation. The novelty is less about a new compression algorithm and more about deriving a common criterion for compression and pruning directly from the terminal prediction objective.f8:T4c7,The experiments are designed to validate the geometry rather than to maximize benchmark scores. Four empirical themes stand out. (1) Perturbation sensitivity: perturbing hidden states along high-eigenvalue directions of the pullback Fisher hurts prediction much more than perturbing along low-curvature or near-null directions, supporting the observable/null decomposition. (2) Layerwise rank allocation: under a fixed total rank budget, allocating rank according to the spectrum of the operator preserves performance better than uniform allocation, suggesting that prediction-relevant dimensionality varies substantially across layers. (3) Structured token pruning: using κ_{ℓ,s} to select tokens is more principled than attention-based heuristics because it directly measures contribution to target-logit curvature. (4) Low-rank student distillation: when student capacity is limited, preserving high-curvature directions helps recover teacher behavior more effectively. The provided full-text excerpt does not include the final result tables or exact model sizes, so it is not safe to quote precise parameter counts or gains. The paper reads more like a mechanism-validation study than a scale-driven benchmark paper.f9:T409,This is a skim paper unless you are specifically interested in representation geometry or loss-aware compression. Start with the introduction and problem setup to lock in three objects: loss-to-go, pullback Fisher, and observable versus prediction-null directions. Then read the theorem/proposition section that connects the local Hessian to the pullback Fisher, paying attention to the assumptions: the approximation is local, tied to low-loss trajectories, and depends on residual terms being small. In the experiments, focus on the perturbation study, rank allocation, token pruning, and student distillation. The most informative figures are the layerwise spectra and the token saliency visualizations showing support on causal ancestors. A 30–45 minute read should be enough for the main ideas. If you want to dig deeper, two good questions are whether the geometry remains stable off-distribution or at higher loss, and how much it overlaps in practice with activation covariance, PCA directions, or attention-based saliency.fa:T4a4,The empirical study uses public Pythia checkpoints at four model sizes, controlled LLaMA-style 70M runs, three initialization families, multiple data arms, optimizer-state records, and frozen-checkpoint interventions. The main observations are consistent measured core magnitude profiles after balancing, successful prediction of pooled-shape departure from field width on held-out runs and data arms, alignment of profiles across projections that share a channel space, and movement of q/k profiles with reassigned RoPE frequencies. Training trajectories show broad early formation followed by component-specific continuation or recession. AdamW second-moment factors align with functional channel spaces. Frozen-checkpoint edits separate an invariant reciprocal balance from a loss-sensitive relative gain: flattening the relative gain increases loss while matrix norms and the balanced core are held fixed, and the effect exceeds Gaussian controls after displacement normalization. The fitting protocol also reports that refitting W/s reproduces the scale ratio within about 0.2% and the shape within about 0.004; over k = 1.17 to 1.25, the relevant Weibull ratio varies by roughly 4%.fb:T422,The task set is tightly checked: 2,436 prompts and 7,308 worked examples are re-derived by an independent solver from the prompt text; 42 test items are used per depth and wording after generation; modular arithmetic uses modulus 7 and repeats distinct problems with different worked examples. The main empirical pattern is that many models concentrate activity in layers just before mid-depth and spread activity in later layers. The strength and location of this pattern vary substantially by model family. Qwen2.5 base models from 0.5B to 7B spread less than the average model across tasks and show concentration in parts of the second half of the network, whereas Llama 1B-8B and OLMo-2 tend to spread in later layers. Post-trained models preserve a large part of their base model’s profile but tend to spread more overall, and this effect is not specific to rising serial demand. The dominant axis of difference is associated with accuracy and heads per layer, but it remains after adjusting for answer entropy and among models with equal head counts.fc:T69f,The authors use a continuous-time interacting-particle formulation where each token state x_i(t) lives on the unit sphere. Self-attention contributes a coupled interaction term determined by the query-key matrix A and value matrix V. The FFN is modeled as an independent control term, a token-wise vector field that does not depend on other tokens. A projection operator keeps the dynamics on the sphere.

The main theorem is a controllability result. For any epsilon > 0, any A and V, and any target point x_0 on the sphere, there exists a choice of FFN parameters such that, for almost all initial conditions, all token trajectories enter and remain in the epsilon-ball around x_0 after finite time. Remarkably, a one-neuron FFN is already sufficient. The proof strategy borrows from opinion dynamics and control: construct an external vector field that points toward the target region and has enough magnitude outside that region to dominate the perturbation induced by self-attention. If the FFN field has a lower bound larger than ||V||_op outside the target neighborhood, it can force synchronization.

The paper also proves a converse statement: there exist A and V such that if the FFN field is uniformly bounded by a value below ||V||_op, then convergence of all tokens to the target cannot be guaranteed. This makes ||V||_op a meaningful threshold. The authors further discuss extensions to multi-head attention and convergence to multiple clusters, not just single-cluster consensus. Compared with prior work that includes FFNs as external fields but does not quantify their relative strength, this paper is more explicit about the balance of power between attention and FFN dynamics.fd:T72d,The method has four stages. First, it defines circuit units at the output-dimension level of Transformer MLP projections, treating each dimension in the gate, up, and down projections as an editable unit. This is finer than layer-level or module-level masking and makes sparse selection feasible. Second, it performs supervised candidate-mask optimization. For prompts where the model fails, the authors construct teacher-corrected responses and freeze the model weights, optimizing only masks over internal units so that the masked computation better supports the corrected answer. The goal here is not to repair the model yet, but to identify which internal units matter for moving from failure toward success. The authors explicitly note that this stage suffers from a mismatch between offline references and free generation. Third, they introduce rollout-guided mask refinement, which is the central contribution. The masked model generates multiple rollouts, and the mask is updated with a group-relative policy-gradient objective using response-level task feedback. Intuitively, units that consistently matter for success or failure under actual generation are reinforced, while units that only look important under teacher forcing are filtered out. Unlike PPO- or GRPO-style updates that directly optimize model parameters, RL here is used to optimize circuit selection. Fourth, the refined mask is pruned into a final sparse circuit, and only the corresponding parameters are fine-tuned for targeted repair. Compared with prior work, the main differences are clear: the target is error localization rather than capability preservation, the localization stage is guided by generation-time RL rather than supervision alone, and the final update is circuit-restricted tuning rather than broad fine-tuning or LoRA over large modules.fe:T531,The evaluation uses two 8B instruction-tuned models: Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The main repair results are reported on math and medical tasks. In math, targeted repair raises GSM8K accuracy from 80% to 91% and improves MATH-500 from 75% to 78%. On GSM8K, RESCUE outperforms a supervised-only interpretable baseline by 4 points and vanilla fine-tuning by 3 points, which is important because it isolates the value of rollout-based mask refinement beyond simple mask discovery. In the medical domain, it also beats vanilla fine-tuning on MedMCQA repair sets, suggesting the method is not restricted to arithmetic. The preservation result is equally important: across eight non-target benchmarks, the repaired models retain 99.4% of baseline aggregate performance on average. That number directly supports the paper’s main claim that local repair can preserve general capabilities. The paper also reports mechanism-oriented evidence: the discovered circuits are sparse, and their causal effects transfer across input rephrasings, which argues against mere template memorization. When reading the experiments, the most informative ablations are the comparison between supervised-only masks and rollout-refined masks, the sparsity or pruning trade-off, and the contrast between local parameter tuning and full fine-tuning.ff:T40e,A good skim starts with the framing in the introduction: this is not generic interpretability, but error attribution tied to targeted repair. Then read the method section with one question in mind: why is supervised mask optimization insufficient, and what exactly does rollout-based refinement recover? After that, jump to the main result tables for GSM8K, MATH-500, MedMCQA, and the non-target retention benchmarks. The deeper questions worth following up are whether RL is best used for circuit localization rather than direct parameter updates, and whether these error circuits transfer to larger models and harder domains such as code or long-horizon reasoning.100:T4e4,Activation-Supported Parameter Decomposition represents a target weight matrix W using rank-1 components. Each component has a read direction v_c, a write direction u_c, and a context-dependent gate g_{t,c}(X). The read direction specifies what information is consumed from the input activation, the write direction specifies the output direction being produced, and the gate determines when the component is active at a token position. Pure parameter decomposition is underdetermined because many decompositions can represent the same matrix. ASPD constrains this ambiguity using the model’s actual activation distribution. Instead of optimizing expensive pairwise interventions between all activation features and all parameter components, it uses a shared sparse representation that both defines activation features and gates the corresponding weight components. A local internal reconstruction objective asks the learned components to reconstruct W x at the output of the analyzed matrix, avoiding reliance on final-output effects alone. This differs from activation-only SAE work and parameter-only decomposition by giving each component an explicit read-write interpretation and making these components composable into parameter-level circuits.101:T9b7,技术路线可以拆成“人类提供什么”和“agent 决定什么”两部分。

人类提供的是 Research Skills。它们不是逐实验的人工指令，而是把专家经验编码成可执行的操作模板、代码资产、权限边界和流程约束。论文强调 high-density prior, low-frequency intervention：人类把成熟做法一次性写成可复用技能，之后不再频繁介入具体实验决策。这样做的目的，是把经验保留在系统里，但把搜索权交给 agent，而不是让 agent 在完全无先验的空间里盲搜。

agent 端由 Codex GPT-5.6-Sol（xhigh reasoning）承担。它从 base checkpoint 和可用算力出发，先构建 executable task pool，再基于 verified capability-gap trajectories 对 Qwen3.6-27B 做 cold-start。随后训练流程不是直接从 SFT 跳到 RL，而是先经过 OPSD，再过渡到 RLVR。根据正文描述，OPSD 阶段里至少发生了三类关键调整：其一，evaluation 会反过来决定哪些数据进入训练，说明数据池不是静态的，而是被在线证据筛选；其二，受控消融改变了 self-teacher 可见的证据范围，作者借此诊断 teacher 何时在利用泄漏信息、何时在学真实能力；其三，原有目标函数出现 collapsing objective，迫使 agent 把学习规则改成 verifier-anchored credit，也就是让 credit assignment 更紧贴可验证结果，而不是依赖容易漂移的代理信号。

RLVR 阶段则处理另一组问题：reward exploits、false verdicts、length-dependent degeneration。对应的修补方向分别是重写 reward eligibility、调整优化过程、控制 trajectory budgeting。这里最值得注意的是，论文没有把 RLVR 写成一个固定 recipe，而是把它描述成一系列失败后的重设计：奖励被利用，就收紧资格；verifier 有误判，就修改奖励语义或过滤机制；长输出导致退化，就把预算和优化目标一起改。这个叙述方式很像真实工业训练，而不是干净的学术设定。

从模型定位看，iCoder-27B 是一个面向工业编码的专门模型，任务覆盖 RTL 设计和 GPU kernel 优化。选择这两个方向有明确原因：它们都能用可执行 verifier 检查正确性，同时又要求性能意识和系统约束，不是普通代码补全就能解决。论文因此把“可验证环境中的 agent-led model development”落在一个反馈足够硬、但搜索空间仍然很大的场景里。102:T749,结果部分最醒目的是 iCoder-27B 在多个工业代码基准上的竞争力。相对同尺寸的 Qwen3.6-27B，iCoder 在 RTLLM 上从 49.6 提升到 68.0，增幅 18.4 分；在 VerilogEval Spec-to-RTL 上从 70.1 提升到 86.3，增幅 16.2 分；在 KernelBench L2 correctness 上从 28 提升到 74，约 2.64 倍。这个幅度说明它不是小修小补，而是任务能力被显著重塑。

论文还给了更贴近使用场景的 case study。对 8 个 RTL design 任务，iCoder 距 HY3 和 DeepSeek-V4-Pro 分别只差 1.1 和 4.5 分，但使用的输出 token 仅为它们报告值的 51% 和 33%。这说明它不仅正确率高，推理开销也更省。对选取的 8 个 GPU operator，它在其中 2 个上达到 strongest archived endpoint，说明其优化能力不只是 benchmark 分数上的偶然。

从全文表述看，实验的另一条主线是开发过程中的 ablation 和失败分析，而不仅是最终榜单。作者强调 evaluation 改变训练数据进入条件、controlled ablation 改变 self-teacher 证据、objective collapse 触发学习规则重写、reward exploit 和 false verdict 改写 RLVR 设计。这些内容如果正文给出具体表格和时间线，会比最终分数更值得看，因为它们揭示了 agent 是如何做研发决策的。103:Ta30,The setup is organized around a division of labor. Humans provide Research Skills: reusable, executable operational procedures, code assets, permission boundaries, and process scaffolds distilled from expert model-development practice. The paper frames this as high-density prior, low-frequency intervention. The point is not to remove human expertise, but to compress it into reusable machinery so that the agent can search over concrete development decisions without requiring constant human steering.

The agent is Codex GPT-5.6-Sol running at high reasoning effort. Starting from a base checkpoint and available compute, it first builds an executable task pool, then cold-starts Qwen3.6-27B on verified capability-gap trajectories. Training does not jump directly from supervised initialization to RL. Instead, the pipeline goes through OPSD and then RLVR.

The OPSD stage appears to be where much of the development logic happens. The paper highlights at least three important dynamics. First, evaluation changes which data are admitted into training, so the data mixture is not static but filtered by ongoing evidence. Second, controlled ablations alter what evidence the self-teacher can access, which is a way to diagnose when the teacher is exploiting leakage versus learning transferable capability. Third, the original objective collapses, forcing the agent to redesign the learning rule around verifier-anchored credit. That means credit assignment is tied more tightly to executable verification rather than to softer proxy signals that drift or become exploitable.

The RLVR stage addresses a different set of failures: reward exploits, false verdicts, and length-dependent degeneration. The corresponding fixes involve changing reward eligibility, modifying optimization behavior, and redesigning trajectory budgeting. One of the strongest aspects of the paper is that RLVR is not presented as a fixed recipe. It is presented as a sequence of failures and revisions: when reward is exploited, tighten eligibility; when the verifier is wrong, revise reward semantics or filtering; when long outputs degrade behavior, adjust both budget and optimization. That is much closer to real model development than a static benchmark loop.

The task domain is industrial coding, specifically RTL design and GPU kernel optimization. That choice is sensible. Both domains offer executable verification, but they also require exact reasoning, systems awareness, and performance-sensitive optimization. This gives the agent a hard feedback signal without collapsing the problem into ordinary code completion.104:T760,The headline results are strong for a 27B model. On KernelBench L2 correctness it rises from 28 to 74, about 2.64x. Those are large deltas, suggesting substantial task-specific capability reshaping rather than marginal tuning.

Equally important is the process evidence described in the paper. Evaluation changes data admission, controlled ablations change self-teacher evidence, objective collapse triggers a redesign of the learning rule, and reward exploits plus false verdicts force RLVR changes.
