But the real value is in the process details: how evaluation feeds back into data selection, why the objective collapses, how verifier-anchored credit is defined, how reward eligibility is tightened, and how length-dependent degeneration is diagnosed and mitigated. The right reading stance is cautious: this is agent-led development under strong human priors and institutional scaffolding, not fully autonomous research without hand-designed structure.106:T907,方法上有四个部分。第一是 Extractor 数据集本身。作者选择一个真实而且不算简单的逆向工程工具作为开发对象：从 Apple Objective-C / Mach-O 二进制中恢复 protobuf descriptor。整个项目 21,000 行生产代码，测试规模相当，210 个 commits，25 个 sessions，678 条用户指令，全部由 Claude 模型生成，没有人工编写代码、测试或 commit。这个设置的价值在于，它不是 toy repo，也不是只截取若干聊天片段，而是完整保留了开发过程。

第二是代码 provenance tracing 工具。作者提出两种追踪方法。其一是基于 control-flow-graph block decomposition 加 git log -L 历史追踪，并处理 rename bridge，用来把代码块级别的变更追溯到具体来源事件。这里的来源不只是用户指令，也包括 AI 的自发发现和自我修正。其二是 session transcript mining，从工具调用日志中恢复那些在 session 内已经被修正、因此不会出现在 commit 历史里的代码生成错误。这个点很关键，因为只看 git history 会低估模型犯错率，尤其低估“先写错、再自救”的频率。

第三是三套 taxonomy。用户指令 taxonomy 扩展了 Tang 等人的 IDE-chat 分类，使其适用于多轮 CLI coding agent 场景，并新增 cross-session coordination 与 correction of AI conduct 两类。commit provenance taxonomy 则把传统软件工程里的 Perfective / Corrective / Adaptive maintenance 进一步拆开，区分“为什么改”和“怎么发现要改”。response reliability taxonomy 是这篇文章最有新意的部分之一：作者不只看代码结果，而是把 AI 对用户的陈述按 reporting / verification、mechanism explanation、root-cause diagnosis、design fix proposal 等类型分类，再用软件工件去核验这些陈述是否准确。

第四是基于上述工具和 taxonomy 的过程分析。作者把开发过程区分为 proactive 与 reactive 两类触发机制，前者是主动扩展、规划、实现，后者是对 bug、测试失败、异常现象的响应。这样做的目的，是理解 AI coding agent 到底是在“持续前进，偶尔修错”，还是“频繁出错，被动补洞”。全文结论偏向前者，但同时指出中间错误并不少。107:T9c8,The work has four technical components. First is the Extractor dataset itself. The target project is a real reverse-engineering tool that recovers protobuf descriptors from Apple Objective-C / Mach-O binaries. It is not a toy repository. The project contains 21,000 lines of production Python code, a similarly sized test suite, 210 commits, 25 sessions, and 678 user instructions. All code, tests, and commits were authored by Claude models, with no human-written code. The value of this setup is completeness: it preserves the full development process rather than a thin slice of it.

Second are two provenance-tracing tools. One combines control-flow-graph block decomposition with git log -L history tracing, including rename bridging, to map code changes back to specific source events. Those events include user instructions, autonomous discoveries, and self-corrections. The other mines session transcripts and tool-use logs to recover code-generation errors that were fixed within a session and therefore never appear in commit history. This is a key methodological point. Commit-only analysis systematically underestimates how often the model first writes something wrong and then repairs it.

Third are three taxonomies. The instruction-intent taxonomy extends Tang et al.’s IDE-chat taxonomy to multi-turn CLI coding-agent interaction and adds categories such as cross-session coordination and correction of the AI’s own conduct. The commit-provenance taxonomy extends the standard Perfective/Corrective/Adaptive maintenance framing by separating why a change was needed from how that need was discovered. The response-reliability taxonomy is one of the more original parts of the paper. Instead of only checking code outcomes, the authors classify the agent’s user-facing claims into categories such as fact reporting, mechanism explanation, root-cause diagnosis, and design-fix proposal, then verify those claims against the software artifacts.

Fourth is the process analysis built on top of these tools. The authors distinguish proactive development from reactive development. Proactive work means planning, extending, and implementing ahead of failures. Reactive work means responding to bugs, failed tests, or observed problems. This framing helps answer whether the agent mostly advances the project and occasionally repairs mistakes, or whether it is mainly patching its own failures. The paper finds more of the former, but with a nontrivial amount of hidden intermediate error.108:T716,The key results come from full-process annotation rather than final-repo statistics. On scale, the project contains 21k lines of production code, a roughly comparable test suite, 210 commits, 25 sessions, and 678 cleaned user instructions. On interaction patterns, CLI-based coding-agent instructions differ from prior IDE-chat datasets by putting more weight on comprehension, planning, and consultation rather than one-shot code requests. On development dynamics, 86–90% of commits and 89–90% of code blocks trace back to proactive triggers rather than reactive responses to bugs or failed tests. In this case study, development is mostly forward-moving rather than purely error-driven.

The most informative numbers are about hidden errors and conversational reliability. By mining transcripts rather than only commits, the authors estimate that 14.3% of AI code-generation events contain a real error that is later caught by the AI-authored test suite before any commit is made. Standard commit-based analysis would miss these errors entirely. For user-facing responses, Claude is relatively reliable when reporting or verifying facts at 94.3% accuracy, somewhat worse when explaining an existing mechanism at 91.1%, lower again for root-cause diagnosis at 89.3%, and substantially weaker when proposing a design fix at 79.4%. Overall, roughly one in four to five interactive responses contains at least one inaccuracy. That result is important because it shows that code generation ability and explanation reliability are related but not interchangeable.

The empirical strength of the paper is not breadth across many repositories. It is traceability. The authors recover intermediate mistakes, temporary hypotheses, and corrected misconceptions that are usually erased from the visible software history.109:Tadc,方法由两部分组成：IterSynth 范式本身，以及配套的 Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization（RDPO）。

先看 IterSynth。它把一次 deep search 拆成 Planner 和 Synthesizer 两个交替角色，但这两个角色不是两套模型，而是同一个 LLM 在不同 role prompt/格式下的两种行为模式。Planner 只看压缩后的 summary state，负责判断还缺什么信息、下一步该搜什么、何时继续探索。Synthesizer 读取新检索到的证据，对 summary 做增量更新：吸收有用事实、处理冲突、丢弃噪声、维护当前结论和未解决问题。这样，summary 不再是外部 memory module 的被动压缩结果，而是 agent policy 的显式输出和持久状态。

这个设计同时解决两个问题。对 role coupling，它通过角色分工降低单步决策的能力混杂度。Planner 不需要在长证据块里写最终答案，Synthesizer 也不需要决定全局搜索策略。对 context accumulation，它不再把完整历史一直塞回上下文，而是让 summary 成为受控、紧凑、可更新的状态表示。相比多 agent 系统，它不需要多模型协作和额外部署复杂度；相比已有 summary-based agent，它把摘要更新纳入训练目标，而不是把 summarization 当外接工具。

再看训练。作者采用 SFT → RL 的两阶段 recipe。SFT 的作用是教会模型 Planner–Synthesizer 协议、角色切换格式和基本迭代搜索行为，但作者明确指出 imitation 只能学会“怎么按这个协议行动”，不能充分优化“什么时候搜、搜什么、保留什么证据、两个角色如何协同”。因此引入 RDPO。

RDPO 的关键不是简单加一个中间奖励，而是按角色做 credit assignment。它把终局 outcome reward 和 turn-level rubric evaluation 结合起来，再分别为 Planner 和 Synthesizer 计算 group-relative advantages。这样做的动机很直接：Planner 的好坏更多体现在 query 是否有信息增益、是否识别到知识缺口、是否避免冗余搜索；Synthesizer 的好坏则体现在证据整合、冲突处理和 summary 更新质量。如果沿用普通 GRPO 或 outcome-only RL，两个角色共享一条回报，梯度会把不同错误来源混在一起，尤其在长轨迹里更严重。RDPO 通过 role-specific advantage 让更新方向更贴近各自职责。

从范式上看，这篇工作和 ReAct 的差异不只是“多了摘要”，而是把搜索过程从线性 action history 改成了围绕 summary state 的迭代闭环。和外部 summarizer 方法相比，它避免了摘要器与主 policy 目标不一致的问题。和多 agent 方法相比，它保留单参数集部署优势，同时通过角色解耦获得部分 specialization 收益。10a:T9f2,The method has two parts: the IterSynth search paradigm and the associated Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization (RDPO) training objective.

IterSynth alternates between two roles, Planner and Synthesizer, instantiated by the same LLM rather than by separate models. The Planner reads only the compact summary state and decides what information is still missing, what to search next, and whether exploration should continue. The Synthesizer reads newly retrieved evidence and updates the persistent summary by integrating useful facts, resolving conflicts, filtering noise, and maintaining the current state of knowledge. In this design, the summary is not an external memory artifact. It is the explicit, learned state of the search process.

This addresses both target problems. Role coupling is reduced because planning and evidence integration are no longer forced into the same local decision. Context accumulation is reduced because the agent no longer carries the full search history forward; it carries a controlled, compact, updateable state instead. Compared with multi-agent systems, this avoids extra models and coordination overhead. Compared with prior summary-based agents, it makes summary updating part of the policy itself rather than an auxiliary external module.

Training follows an SFT-to-RL recipe. SFT teaches the Planner–Synthesizer protocol, role formatting, and basic iterative search behavior. But the authors explicitly note that imitation mainly teaches the interaction pattern, not the deeper decisions of when to search, what evidence to preserve, or how the two roles should coordinate. That is why they introduce RDPO.

RDPO combines terminal outcome rewards with turn-level rubric evaluations and computes group-relative advantages separately for Planner and Synthesizer actions. The motivation is straightforward: the Planner should be rewarded for identifying information gaps, issuing informative queries, and avoiding redundant exploration, while the Synthesizer should be rewarded for evidence integration, conflict handling, and summary quality. Standard outcome-only GRPO mixes these error sources together, which is especially harmful in long trajectories. Role-specific advantages make the gradient signal better aligned with each role’s responsibility.

Conceptually, the difference from ReAct is not just the addition of summaries. IterSynth changes the search loop from a linear action history into an iterative process centered on an explicit summary state. That is the main modeling contribution.10b:T60c,The headline result is that IterSynth-8B reaches 50.7% average performance across five long-horizon deep-search benchmarks: GAIA-text-only, xBench-2505, xBench-2510, BrowseComp, and BrowseComp-ZH. This is 4.2 points above the strongest prior agent at 8B or below, while remaining competitive with several 30B-scale agents at less than one third of the parameter budget.

The training ablations are particularly informative. The SFT baseline scores 44.1%. Outcome-only GRPO raises this to 48.9%. RDPO further improves it to 50.7%. So RL itself contributes a large gain, and role-decoupled credit assignment adds another 1.8 points on top. The paper notes that this extra gain is strongest on exploration-heavy benchmarks, which suggests that RDPO improves search behavior rather than only answer polishing.

A key diagnostic appears in Appendix H: even with a 64K context window, more than 59% of ReAct trajectories on BrowseComp fail to terminate before context exhaustion. This directly supports the paper’s claim that the bottleneck is not simply context length, but the way search state is represented and updated.

The prompting-transfer results are also useful. IterSynth is not only a trainable 8B-agent recipe; it also works as a prompting paradigm for frontier models such as Claude-4.5-Opus and DeepSeek-V3.1, consistently outperforming ReAct and IterResearch, with gains of up to 10 points over ReAct on BrowseComp-ZH. That suggests the paradigm captures a generally better search organization rather than a narrow model-specific trick.10c:T42b,Start with the Introduction and Figure 1. The paper clearly contrasts three paradigms: multi-agent decomposition, external summarization, and IterSynth. Once that structural difference is clear, the rest of the method becomes much easier to follow.

Then read the methodology in two passes. First, focus on what each role sees and produces, and how the summary state is updated. Second, study RDPO carefully, especially why advantages are computed separately by role instead of using a single GRPO-style return for the whole trajectory. If you have worked on agent RL before, this is the part where the paper’s real contribution becomes obvious.

In the experiments, prioritize the main benchmark table, the ablations, and Appendix H. The main table answers whether the method works, the ablations explain why, and Appendix H shows where ReAct actually breaks. If time is limited, read the average benchmark results, the SFT → GRPO → RDPO progression, and the prompting-transfer section. A quick pass takes under an hour; a careful read takes around 90 minutes.10d:T412,TRACER uses a two-stage training recipe. First, supervised fine-tuning on real user dialogues teaches the model to generate user responses and to emit structured annotations: a rationale and an ordinal intent score. The intent score acts as an interpretable proxy for the user’s evolving commitment or engagement state. Second, the simulator is trained with multi-turn reinforcement learning while interacting with a fixed assistant. Rewards combine terminal outcome agreement and trajectory alignment against paired human logs. Dynamic time warping is used to align trajectories with different lengths and conversational pacing. A deviation-aware advantage modulation mechanism then uses local alignment errors, accumulated over discounted trajectory suffixes, to scale turn-level policy updates while preserving the direction of the session-level advantage. Compared with static persona prompting, the method optimizes state evolution; compared with standard turn-level optimization, it assigns credit using the whole dialogue trajectory.10e:T4a1,TalkMesh places agents on a sparse communication graph. Each agent uses a frozen base model M with two LoRA adapters: a confidence head V and a talk policy T. Inference has five stages. First, agents independently sample proposals, matching the independence assumption of self-consistency. Second, V scores each proposal using the sigmoid of the Yes-versus-No logit gap under a fixed verification prompt. Third, the highest-confidence agent becomes the speaker and emits a hint capped at 112 tokens. Fourth, listeners whose confidence is below 0.5, or who did not produce an answer, revise their proposals using the hint. A revision is accepted only if V scores it higher than the original. Fifth, agents run gossip consensus to approximate a centralized confidence-weighted vote without a coordinator. The confidence head is trained as an outcome verifier. The talk policy is trained inside the protocol with GRPO using a flip reward: +1 when a revision changes a wrong answer to a correct one, and -1 for the reverse. The speaker receives the mean flip reward over its listeners. Training uses a curriculum over rollout size K = 3, 5, and 8, while evaluation scales to larger meshes.10f:T402,The main experiments compare self-consistency, confidence reranking without messages, and the trained mesh. With three agents, the trained mesh reaches the accuracy of self-consistency with 32 samples. At N = 32, SmolLM3-3B on MATH-500 improves from 0.492 under self-consistency to 0.722 with TalkMesh, while reranking without messages reaches 0.590. Qwen3.5-0.8B on GSM8K improves from 0.568 to 0.705, with reranking at 0.655. In an attack setting with N = 8 and four compromised agents submitting the same wrong answer with claimed confidence 0.99, majority vote drops to 0.000 on 150 test problems. The defended mesh, which rescores solutions and gates revisions, retains 0.507 on Qwen3.5-0.8B GSM8K versus 0.667 without attack; an undefended version drops to at most 0.007. Additional evaluations cover SwarmBench and traffic control. On the severe traffic subset, messages reduce person delay for Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2B, and 4B meshes by 23.6±6.7 seconds; over all 70 scenarios, the 4B mesh reduces delay by 11.4±6.9 seconds.110:T423,The starting point is Karpathy’s AutoResearch loop: an LLM edits training code, launches an experiment, and keeps changes that improve a held-out metric. The authors deploy this pattern in two production representation-learning systems at Amazon and identify five recurring failure modes: infrastructure fragility, agent memory decay, search-direction stagnation, iteration-cost asymmetry, and metric fixation. The proposed scaffolding follows three principles. Prevent uses a semantic gate before execution, which is worthwhile when a failed run wastes many GPU-hours. Persist stores durable cross-job memory, so the agent does not repeat known mistakes or forget prior findings during multi-week campaigns. Redirect triggers strategic reframing when local code or hyperparameter edits stop producing progress. The implementation is a three-agent extension of AutoResearch. The main design lesson is cost dependence: expensive iterations justify heavier pre-run checks, while cheaper iterations can rely more on post-run revert and lightweight supervision.111:T43b,The system implements agentic meta-reasoning: reasoning about the agent’s own computation before dispatching more computation. Workers perform task-level work. A controller maintains a compact account of the run, proposes possible next computations, evaluates their value under the remaining budget, and sends selected assignments to workers with only the relevant retrieved artifacts. Full outputs are stored in persistent memory as artifacts with stable identifiers. The controller’s private state is rewritten at each control cycle and does not have to include the full history. Each cycle has four stages: state update, option generation, option evaluation, and dispatch. The design differs from a simple ReAct-style loop or direct-control agent because control is not a single next-action prediction conditioned on the accumulated transcript. Control itself is an agentic process with memory access and intermediate outputs. The artifact graph records which artifact was used to produce which later artifact, giving a structural trace of branching, reuse, and failure modes.112:T432,The evaluation spans IMO ProofBench-Advanced, ARC-AGI-2, LongCoT-mini, and ProgramBench, covering proof search, abstract reasoning, long-horizon reasoning, and program reconstruction. The models include Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5, and Opus 4.8. The main budgets are 100 model calls for the reasoning benchmarks and 1200 calls for ProgramBench. Baselines include production coding agents, research harnesses, and a Direct Control Agent that keeps workers and available actions fixed while replacing the controller with a single-step decision over accumulated history. At the main budgets, meta-reasoning has higher point estimates in all 12 matched comparisons, with average gains of about 3.6 to 4.2 score points by benchmark. On ProgramBench with GPT-5.5, mean per-problem test-pass rate reaches 71.5%, compared with 58.0% for Codex and 63.7% for direct control. Scaling curves show continued improvement with larger budgets, while direct control tends to plateau. Artifact-graph analysis shows more reuse of earlier work and more runs in which a correct candidate is present.113:T633,The design is simple and distinctive. A standard LM updates context by concatenation, while a CLM is allowed to apply an arbitrary transformation to context at each step. Concretely, the live context is mirrored into a file. The model can either generate normally or use tools such as Bash to edit the context file directly, and the edited file is immediately synchronized back into the next-turn context. This enables in-place updates, deletion of stale information, maintenance of structured trackers, internal notes, and explicit working memory. The same abstraction extends naturally to multi-agent settings, where multiple context files can coexist for subagents or swarms. The paper also addresses the serving side. It introduces prefix-reuse FLOPs as a trajectory-level compute metric that accounts for decoding, prefilling, and re-prefilling under standard serving when in-the-middle edits break prefix matching. It then proposes Suffix Cache Reuse (SCR), which attempts to reuse cache beyond the matching prefix after edits, reducing re-prefill cost while preserving empirical task quality. For training, the authors use stepwise GRPO with a success-gated efficiency advantage: only successful trajectories compete on efficiency, which is important because naive token-minimization rewards would otherwise encourage over-compression and information loss. Finally, the paper introduces ContextBench, a diagnostic benchmark that isolates context management from reasoning and knowledge by testing selective retention, exact in-place updates, KV-style storage, and log maintenance.114:T5a1,The empirical story is broad and fairly concrete. On ContextBench, CLMs outperform summary-based and action-constrained baselines on synthetic tasks such as Needle Retention, Sudoku Sketchpad, KV Store, and Log Triage, showing stronger selective retention and exact editing behavior. On real long-horizon tasks, CLMs do well both in quality and compute. On BrowseComp-Plus, they achieve 11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs than the strongest baseline. On TerminalBench 2.1, they match the best baseline’s accuracy while using 29.5% fewer FLOPs. On a 12-hour subset of EdgeBench, they score 5% higher with 59% fewer FLOPs. On a 24-hour six-repository agent-swarm task, they deliver 65% greater end-to-end speedup at the same compute budget. On mathematical optimization, they outperform specialized evolutionary harnesses such as OpenEvolve by up to 16.8% on Heilbronn and 3.0% on circle packing. The RL result is also notable: training Qwen3.5-9B with the proposed stepwise GRPO setup improves BrowseComp-Plus from 28.8% to 42.5%, beating a Codex-style summary harness trained with the same recipe by 0.4 points while using 38.8% fewer FLOPs. On the systems side, adding SCR reduces server-side compute by another 35% at matched performance relative to standard SGLang serving. These numbers suggest that the gains are not just from adding tools, but from letting the model learn finer-grained state editing policies.115:T50b,Although tagged as skim, this is worth a closer read if you care about long context, memory, agent systems, or the pretrain/post-train boundary. Start with the formal contrast between standard LM updates and CLM updates. Then read the ContextBench section early, because it makes the failure modes of summary/retrieval-style context management very concrete. After that, go to the real-task experiments and track two metrics together: task success and prefix-reuse FLOPs. Looking only at accuracy misses a large part of the paper’s claim, which is that better context management lowers total inference cost. In the training section, focus on the definition and ablations of the success-gated efficiency advantage to see whether it really avoids pathological compression. In the systems section, inspect the assumptions behind Suffix Cache Reuse and why suffix reuse after middle edits does not noticeably hurt performance. A solid first pass takes about an hour. The deeper questions are whether the benefit mostly comes from the interface rather than new model capability, whether such editing behavior can be learned during pretraining rather than only post-training, and whether file-based context is a temporary bridge toward more explicit state-space or external-memory architectures.116:T420,The central mechanism is ResearchSpec, a compact executable specification of what the final report must establish. Multiple Planning Writers independently search and read sources, then propose candidate structures. A Planning Judge consolidates them, a Critic looks for missing questions and cases, and a Reviser folds the feedback back into the specification. ResearchSpec stores each section’s scope, research questions, required entities or cases, provisional source leads, and hierarchical section IDs. Validators check ID uniqueness, parent-child consistency, consecutive ordering, and required fields before dispatch. Each Researcher then receives the full ResearchSpec plus one section assignment, conducts further evidence gathering in an independent context, and writes a complete section. The assembled draft is reviewed by a Global Editor, while Local Editors apply targeted revisions to affected sections. The design trades some flexibility for controllability: the plan is refined before dispatch and then held fixed during section research.117:T6bf,The system has three parts. The first is a persistent context graph. Instead of storing history as a flat sequence of messages, the system keeps messages, tool calls, and full tool results as persistent nodes, preserving chronology and references. This matters because omitted results are not destroyed; they remain recoverable later.

The second is Tool-Flow Analysis (TFA), which is the main technical idea. TFA tracks how values introduced by earlier tool results are reused in later model steps and tool calls. When a later operation uses a value that originated in an earlier result, the system records an execution dependency and treats it as observed reuse. This is different from standard retrieval memory: the signal is not only whether an old chunk looks relevant to the current query, but whether the execution trace has already shown that the old result supports later actions.

The third is the renderer. Before each model invocation, it selects which historical tool results to expose within a fixed token budget. Selection combines three signals: observed reuse, recency, and semantic relevance. Unselected results stay in the graph and can be restored later. This is a more conservative design than aggressive summarization, because summaries often discard details whose importance only becomes clear much later.

A notable design choice is that the paper does not rely on a learned memory controller or model-driven compression policy. It uses explicit structured state plus hand-designed signals. The upside is interpretability and recoverability. The limitation is that TFA will only be as good as its ability to detect value flow; abstract semantic reuse is likely harder than literal or near-literal reuse.118:T4e1,The evaluation uses two benchmarks, AppWorld and 8-objective QA, with three execution models. The main setting allocates a 6K history budget for prior execution steps rather than passing the full accumulated history. Under this budget, ContextRender reaches task performance close to, and sometimes above, full-history prompting while reducing mean standardized inference cost by 10.2% to 32.2% relative to full history.

Against managed-context baselines, it delivers the best overall task performance across both benchmarks and all three models in the primary setting. The main point is not a single benchmark number, but the fact that it remains competitive under a much smaller visible history budget while preserving recoverability of omitted full results.

The ablations are the most informative part. Adding observed reuse on top of recency and semantic relevance improves both task performance and recall of results that are reused later. The gains are especially large for results reused after long gaps. That directly supports the paper’s claim: long-range execution dependencies are poorly handled by recency-only heuristics, and semantic relevance alone can undervalue tool outputs dominated by identifiers, paths, or parameter values.119:T4b9,The paper contributes a measurement framework and a clean counterfactual design. First, it operationalizes factionalism through interaction traces. In each round, every agent makes an observable commitment and sends that commitment plus a short message to selected peers. From this trace, the authors build a directed weighted agreement graph. An edge from agent i to agent j gains weight when j's next-round commitment matches the commitment that i sent to j. The normalization is important: it controls for contact frequency and convergence timing, so the metric reflects alignment conditional on communication rather than raw message volume.

Second, the experimental design isolates label effects from model effects. The same underlying agents and tasks are run under different visible-label conditions: true family labels, shuffled family labels, neutral labels such as colors, and no visible identity. This is the core methodological move. It separates clustering caused by actual model differences from clustering caused by the mere presence of a label. The reported outcome is that the grouping follows the visible label, including shuffled and neutral labels, rather than the underlying model family.11a:T543,FlowMAS models workflow construction as trajectory generation with a GFlowNet. A state corresponds to a partially built workflow topology, actions extend the topology, and a terminal state is a complete workflow. The GFlowNet is trained so that terminal workflows are sampled in proportion to their rewards, which encourages a distribution over high-reward candidates rather than a single optimized graph.

The paper adds two components on top of a vanilla GFlowNet. The information-guided module uses Partial Information Decomposition to estimate how different operators contribute unique, redundant, and synergistic information toward the task. This gives more structured credit assignment than a single scalar textual critique. The curiosity-driven module rewards structural novelty, pushing the generator to explore underrepresented workflow patterns and reducing collapse to a few templates.

Compared with search-based systems such as ADAS and AFlow, FlowMAS learns a reusable topology generator instead of repeatedly searching a large tree. Compared with textual-gradient methods such as OneFlow and DebFlow, it aims for finer-grained structural feedback. Compared with VAE, graph diffusion, or MLP-based generators, the paper argues that GFlowNets are a better fit for discrete graph-like objects with reward-driven diversity requirements.11b:T70a,The paper analyzes discrete heavy-ball momentum dynamics in a river-valley model of the loss landscape. The geometry is decomposed into a low-loss, low-curvature, slowly bending river manifold and sharp orthogonal valley directions. The optimization challenge is not merely to descend, but to move quickly along the river without letting oscillations in the sharp directions destabilize the trajectory.

The main result is that momentum enlarges the largest tolerable learning rate by a leading factor of roughly (1+β)/(1-β) relative to vanilla GD. This factor is classical for quadratic objectives, but the nontrivial part here is showing that it still governs the leading stability threshold in a non-convex setting where the river and valley subspaces rotate and interact over time. Because of that rotation, gradient and momentum components leak across subspaces, so one cannot reuse a fixed-eigenspace argument.

To handle this, the authors develop a new inductive analysis that tracks both gradient and momentum projections onto river and valley directions, while controlling their mutual interference across iterations. A second key conclusion is interpretive: for a flat and slowly spinning river, momentum itself does not substantially change the intrinsic speed along the river. The acceleration mainly comes from enabling a much larger stable learning rate. In that sense, momentum acts more as a stabilizer that permits aggressive step sizes than as a direct source of extra river-direction acceleration.

The paper also improves the largest tolerable learning-rate bound for vanilla GD in the same river-valley framework. That side result suggests the proof machinery is not narrowly tailored to momentum alone, but strengthens the analytical understanding of the landscape model itself.11c:T5fb,From the available full-text content, this is primarily a theory paper, with experiments serving to validate the mechanism rather than to establish a new large-scale training recipe. The empirical phenomenon tied to the theory is clear: under WSD-like schedules, a long high-LR phase can produce higher observed loss than cosine scheduling because of oscillations across sharp valley walls, while still making faster progress along the river. Once the learning rate is sharply decayed, those oscillations are suppressed and the hidden progress becomes visible as a lower final loss.

The paper also mentions synthetic river-valley loss constructions for visualization and connects its analysis to prior probing of LLM pretraining landscapes in Wen et al. (2025). The most important empirical checks are therefore: (1) momentum remains stable at larger learning rates on synthetic river-valley landscapes; (2) the predicted stability-threshold enlargement matches the observed stable region; and (3) the seemingly paradoxical pattern of higher intermediate loss but better final optimization can be explained by separating river progress from valley oscillation.

The provided text does not include full tables, model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact improvement numbers, so those should not be invented. When reading the original, the most useful experimental artifacts to extract are the stability-boundary plots, the comparisons against vanilla GD, and any quantitative alignment between the theorem and observed training dynamics.11d:T58c,Read it in the order of phenomenon, model, theorem, then proof technique.

Start with the introduction and lock onto the practical question: why can a long high-LR phase plus sharp decay outperform smoother schedules, and what role does momentum play there? Then jump to Theorem 4.1. That is the central statement of the paper: the maximum stable learning rate is enlarged by about (1+β)/(1-β).

After that, spend time on Lemma 5.1 and the surrounding proof structure. This is where the real novelty sits. The important part is not only the final factor, but how the authors control dynamics when the river and valley subspaces rotate and when gradient and momentum components interfere with each other. While reading, focus on three things: how the river/valley projections are defined and updated, what assumptions encode “flat” and “slow-spinning,” and how the error terms are prevented from accumulating into instability.

If time is limited, read the theorem statements, proof sketches, and the main figures first, then return to the technical induction details. Also check the remark on the improved vanilla-GD learning-rate bound; it helps assess whether the analytical framework has broader value beyond the momentum case.

A careful read will likely take 1.5 to 2.5 hours. For readers focused on training stability and optimizer dynamics, this is worth reading with equations and figures side by side.11e:T7f3,技术上分三层。第一层是机制定位。作者从 softmax backward 的标准形式 dS = P ⊙ (dP - δ) 出发，其中每一行的 δ_i = Σ_j P_ij dP_ij，本来保证 dS 每行求和为 0，这对应 softmax 对行平移不变。FP8 attention 的常见实现为了省算，会用保存下来的输出 O 来近似这个 row correction，即 δ_i^stale = <dO_i, Ô_i>。在高精度或前后向操作数一致时，这个捷径成立；但在 FP8 下，forward 用的是量化后的 P、V 得到 Ô，backward 又用重新量化后的 dO、V 得到 dP̂，两边的量化误差来源不同，导致 δ_i^stale 不再等于真正与 dP̂ 匹配的 correction。

第二层是误差如何影响训练。作者推导出 stale delta 会让 dS 的每一行出现非零残差 ε_i = Σ_j dS_ij^stale。这个残差不是无害的，因为它等价于在 matched gradient 上额外加了 ε_i P_ij 这一项。若 ε_i<0，会推动该行 logits 变尖；若 ε_i>0，会推动其变平。表面上看，不同行的残差可能互相抵消，但映射到 channel 维度后并不会自然抵消。作者观察到某些被“偏爱”的通道会持续受到同向压力，尤其体现在 key 侧 RMSNorm gain 被系统性推高，随后形成选择性放大，训练越久越明显。

第三层是修复方法 Delta-Matching。核心思想不是简单提高某个张量精度，而是让 backward row correction 使用与 backward 真实乘法路径一致的量。作者从未量化的 softmax 概率 P 和由 FP8 backward operands 在 FP32 中相乘得到的 dP̂ 出发，重新构造匹配的 δ，使 softmax gradient 的零行和不变量在给定数值假设下恢复。文中还特别说明，只把 dO 保留成 BF16 并不够，因为概率量化带来的不一致仍在。Delta-Matching 的价值在于它不依赖额外保存一个高精度 forward output，也不要求改 attention 结构；它针对的是 backward correction 这个具体失配点，因此可以直接嵌入 native block-scaled FP8 attention kernel。11f:T822,实验设计比较扎实，重点不只是“最终分数更高”，而是把失效边界画出来了。首先在机制验证上，作者拿 1.67B GDN/GQA 训练末期 checkpoint 的 BF16 重算激活，去探测 FP8 kernel 在 6 个 attention layer、32 个训练窗口上的行为。结果显示，在 dS 量化之前，stale delta 造成的归一化 row-sum residual 中位数大约在 1.1e-2 到 4.7e-2，这已经不是可忽略的舍入噪声量级。

规模实验覆盖 569M、1.67B、5.29B。569M 上，stale-delta hybrid 只表现为较温和的 validation loss gap，下游任务大体还能保住；这解释了为什么一些早期工作在 sub-billion 规模上看起来“FP8 attention 也能训”。但到 1.67B 和 5.29B，训练前期还能跟住 BF16/FP32 mixed-precision reference，之后 loss 开始持续抬升，并带来下游性能下降，而且 5.29B 更早出现拐点，符合“误差积累且随规模加速”的判断。

作者还测试了多种可能的缓解手段。QK normalization 能减轻甚至避免某些配置下的灾难性崩溃，但仍留有明显性能差距；NoPE 在保留位置敏感 recurrent 层时只能延后退化；head dimension 从 128 提到 256 没有根治作用。这些结果说明问题不是某个架构细节偶然触发，而是 attention backward 数值约束被破坏后的普遍现象。

在架构泛化上，作者不只测标准 attention，还测了 Gated DeltaNet + MLA 的 hybrid，以及 KDA + GQA 的组合，stale-delta failure 都存在。在线性层精度、模型结构、训练阶段变化下，Delta-Matching 都能把训练 loss 和整体下游表现拉回到 BF16/FP32 mixed-precision attention reference 附近。

长上下文实验也很关键。按 Kimi K2 / DeepSeek-V3 风格 recipe，从 8K 扩到 64K，并把学习率降下来后，stale-delta baseline 相对 BF16/FP32 的 training-loss gap 要到大约 19k optimizer steps、约 20B tokens 后才超过 0.01。这个结果很有信息量：如果只做短程 context extension 验证，很容易误判为“方法没问题”。120:T7df,The technical story has three parts. First, the paper localizes the failure. Softmax backward has the form dS = P ⊙ (dP - δ), where δ_i = Σ_j P_ij dP_ij for each row. In exact arithmetic this guarantees that each row of dS sums to zero, reflecting softmax shift invariance. Many efficient implementations reuse the saved forward output O to compute the row correction, using δ_i^stale = <dO_i, O_hat_i>. This shortcut is valid when the forward and backward quantities are numerically consistent. Under FP8, however, O_hat comes from quantized forward operands, while dP_hat is formed from separately quantized backward operands. The two paths no longer match, so the shortcut becomes stale.

Second, the paper analyzes how this mismatch affects optimization. The stale correction induces a nonzero row residual ε_i = Σ_j dS_ij^stale. That residual adds an extra term ε_i P_ij to the matched gradient. Negative ε_i sharpens a row of logits; positive ε_i flattens it. Even if row-wise residuals nearly cancel globally, they do not cancel channel-wise after projection through Q/K/V. The authors show persistent pressure on selected channels, especially visible as systematic upward drift in key-side RMSNorm gains. This creates selective amplification over training rather than zero-mean noise.

Third, the proposed fix is Delta-Matching. The key idea is to compute the backward row correction from quantities that are actually consistent with the backward path: unquantized softmax probabilities P and FP32 products formed from the FP8 backward operands. Under the stated numerical assumptions, this restores the zero-row-sum invariant. The paper also shows that simply keeping dO in BF16 is insufficient, because the mismatch caused by probability quantization remains. Delta-Matching is attractive because it does not require storing an auxiliary high-precision forward output and does not depend on architectural changes. It directly patches the numerical inconsistency at the backward correction step.121:T81e,The experiments are strong because they map out the failure regime instead of only reporting end metrics. For mechanism validation, the authors probe the FP8 kernel using BF16-recomputed activations from final 1.67B GDN/GQA checkpoints, across six attention layers and 32 training windows. Before dS quantization, stale delta produces normalized row-sum residuals around 1.1e-2 to 4.7e-2 on average row medians over nonzero-gradient rows. That is far above negligible rounding noise.

The scale study covers 569M, 1.67B, and 5.29B models. At 569M, stale-delta hybrid training shows only a modest validation-loss gap and largely preserves downstream quality. This helps explain why earlier small-scale studies could appear encouraging. At 1.67B and 5.29B, however, stale-delta runs initially track BF16/FP32 references, then diverge later with rising loss and degraded downstream performance. The onset is earlier at 5.29B, consistent with cumulative error that accelerates with scale.

The paper also tests several mitigations. QK normalization can prevent catastrophic collapse in some settings, but it still leaves a substantial performance gap. NoPE delays degradation but does not remove it. Increasing head dimension from 128 to 256 does not solve the problem either. This is useful because it shows the issue is not an artifact of one architecture choice.

Generality is tested beyond a single attention design. The stale-delta failure appears in hybrids combining Gated DeltaNet with MLA, and KDA with GQA. Across architectures, training stages, and linear-layer precision settings, Delta-Matching recovers training loss and overall downstream performance close to BF16/FP32 mixed-precision attention references.

The long-context extension result is especially informative. Using a Kimi K2 / DeepSeek-V3 style recipe to extend from 8K to 64K with a lower learning rate, the stale-delta baseline does not exceed a 0.01 training-loss gap over BF16/FP32 until roughly 19k optimizer steps, about 20B tokens. This shows why short extension runs can miss the problem entirely.122:T559,Start with Sections 3.2 to 3.4. The main thing to understand is why the zero-row-sum property is not a cosmetic identity but the backward expression of softmax shift invariance, and why the saved-output shortcut breaks under FP8. Then read Figure 3 carefully. It is the bridge from local numerical inconsistency to long-horizon optimization damage, especially the channel-selective amplification story. After that, go to the scale and context-extension experiments in Section 4, focusing on the contrast between 569M, 1.67B, and 5.29B, and on the delayed failure during 8K to 64K extension.

Two details are worth extra attention. First, the paper shows that matching output-gradient precision alone is not enough. That is a broader lesson for low-precision training: local precision patches often fail if forward and backward are still inconsistent at the algorithmic level. Second, the mitigation results for QK norm and NoPE are useful because they separate error sensitivity from error source. They make training less fragile, but they do not repair the broken invariant.

For a fast read, spend most time on the derivation of stale delta, Figure 3, and the 1.67B main pretraining results. For implementation or reproduction, the appendices matter because the numerical assumptions and residual definitions are important to interpret the proof and the measurements.123:T8e9,实验部分信息量比较足，且不只停留在 ImageNet 分类。

1. 视觉监督训练：作者用约 1M 参数的 core 去初始化 85M 参数的 ViT-Base，再在 ImageNet-1K 上训练，top-1 相比随机初始化提升 +2.2 个百分点。这是最核心的 headline result，因为它说明一个很小的 recurrent core 可以迁移到大得多的目标模型，并带来稳定收益。

2. 下游表征质量：论文没有把收益局限在分类，而是检查了更能反映表征结构的任务。给出的数字包括：ADE20K 语义分割 mIoU 从 26.6 提升到 28.8；ImageNet-S 零样本分割 mAP 从 32.3 到 42.9；VOC07 目标定位 CorLoc 从 9.9 到 18.4；NYUv2 深度估计 RMSE 从 1.104 降到 0.998。这里的模式很重要：定位、分割、深度都变好，说明初始化影响的不只是分类头适配，而是中间表征更规整。

5. 机制分析：作者发现 recurrence 带来的参数共享会把计算分布到更广的方向集合，尤其包含低能量成分；在 ViT 中，结构主要集中在 attention value/output pathway，并能抑制高范数 token outlier。这个分析很关键，因为初始化论文常见问题是“有效但说不清为什么”，而这里至少给出了一条可检验的机制链路。

如果回到预训练视角，最值得核对的细节是：语言模型实验的规模、token 数、训练步数、与 procedural warm-up 本身相比的差距有多大，以及收益是否主要体现在早期收敛还是最终 loss 也持续更优。当前片段没有完整表格，这些数字需要看原文。124:T7c0,The method is called Procedural Core. It has two stages.

Stage one trains a very small recurrent auxiliary transformer on procedural data instead of warming up each target model directly. The auxiliary model is a minimal recurrent ViT with only three unique blocks: an input block, a recurrent middle block, and an output block. The objective and procedural data setup follow prior procedural warm-up work. The key idea is not to maximize the auxiliary model’s standalone performance, but to force useful computation into a compact reusable parameter set through depth-wise sharing. Recurrence acts as a compression mechanism: if deep transformers partly implement block-recurrent programs, then a recurrent model is a natural place to store that structure compactly.

Stage two expands this compact core into a target transformer of arbitrary width and depth. Depth is handled by unrolling the recurrent block across layers. Width is handled by tiling or expansion rules that map the smaller learned weights into a wider model. The result is a deterministic initialization procedure, not a new warm-up run for each target architecture.

The novelty has three layers. First, it turns procedural pretraining from a repeated training stage into a reusable initialization asset. Second, it uses recurrence as the transfer format, rather than directly interpolating or transplanting warm-up weights. Third, the paper goes beyond reporting gains and studies why the method transfers: depth-wise sharing appears to spread computation across a broader set of directions, including lower-energy components that matter for transfer; in ViTs, the strongest effects concentrate in the attention value/output pathway and suppress high-norm token outliers.

From an LLM perspective, the most interesting part is that the same idea is tested not only in vision but also in natural language and code modeling, which argues for a more general transformer prior rather than a vision-specific trick.125:T894,The experimental section is substantial and goes well beyond ImageNet classification.

1. Supervised vision training: a roughly 1M-parameter core is expanded to initialize an 85M-parameter ViT-Base, then trained on ImageNet-1K. This gives a +2.2 point top-1 improvement over random initialization. This is the central result because it shows that a very small recurrent core can transfer to a much larger target model.

2. Representation-sensitive downstream tasks: the gains are not limited to classification. Reported numbers include ADE20K semantic segmentation improving from 26.6 to 28.8 mIoU, ImageNet-S zero-shot segmentation from 32.3 to 42.9 mAP, VOC07 localization from 9.9 to 18.4 CorLoc, and NYUv2 depth estimation improving from 1.104 to 0.998 RMSE. This pattern matters: segmentation, localization, and depth all improve, which suggests the initialization changes internal representations rather than only helping classifier fitting.

3. Self-supervised and cross-domain transfer: the paper also reports gains for DINO, so the effect is not tied to supervised labels. More importantly, the method also helps language models trained on FineWeb-Edu and code models trained on CodeParrot. The excerpt does not expose exact language-model loss or perplexity numbers, but this is what separates the work from a standard CV initialization paper.

4. Baselines: Procedural Core beats both random initialization and structured initialization baselines such as Trockman and Kolter (2023). So the result is not just “any non-random start helps.”

5. Mechanistic analysis: the paper argues that recurrence spreads useful computation across a wider set of directions, especially lower-energy ones, and that in ViTs the effect concentrates in the attention value/output pathway while suppressing high-norm token outliers. This is important because initialization papers often stop at empirical gains; here there is at least a plausible mechanism to inspect.

For pretraining readers, the main missing details to verify in the full paper are the language-model scales, token budgets, training lengths, and how close this gets to running a full procedural warm-up directly on the target model.126:T60e,This deserves more than a quick skim if you care about initialization, data efficiency, procedural data, or the idea that pretraining effects might be compressible into a parameter prior. Start with the introduction and make the distinction from prior procedural warm-up work precise: the goal is not another warm-up stage, but a reusable core that captures its benefit.

Then read the method section carefully, especially the figure and the part describing the three unique blocks, recurrent training, and the expansion rules in depth and width. The key conceptual question is why recurrence should be a better carrier of transferable structure than simply training a small feed-forward transformer.

In the experiments, first read the ImageNet result, then the segmentation/localization/depth evaluations, because those are stronger evidence that the initialization changes representation quality. After that, check the language and code experiments to judge whether the method is truly transformer-general. Finally, read the mechanistic analysis around low-energy directions, the attention value/output pathway, and token-outlier suppression. That section is not the final word, but it gives concrete handles for follow-up work.

A focused read will take around 45 minutes. The most useful follow-up questions are: how the gains scale with model size, how much is lost relative to running a full procedural warm-up on the target model, and whether this initialization interacts with tokenizer choice, data curriculum, or training cooldown recipes.127:T981,技术核心是把当前层的 full weight gradient 分解成 LoRA 可访问部分和不可访问部分。对注入 LoRA 的线性层，设有效权重为 W_base + sBA。给定当前 batch 的输入激活 X 和反向信号 δ，完整权重梯度可恢复为 G_raw = δ^T X（按文中记号，batch 和 token 维展平后计算）。作者证明，由当前 A、B 的欧氏梯度所诱导出来的等价权重空间梯度，恰好张成当前 LoRA 参数化的 tangent space，也就是所谓 LoRA-accessible gradient space。于是可以把 G_raw 正交分解为切空间内的分量和法向分量；后者被称为 normal gradient。

这个 normal gradient 有两个关键性质。第一，只要它非零，取其负方向，在固定当前 adapter 与其他权重的局部条件下，是当前 batch loss 的下降方向。第二，它与当前 LoRA 一阶可达的所有方向都正交，因此不是通过改 adapter 学习率、初始化或梯度重标定就能补回来的。这也是作者为什么不继续做 LoRA factor 的优化修补，而是直接把 normal 分量用于更新 base weights。

GDLoRA 的实现分成两条支路：adapter branch 仍然是标准 LoRA + AdamW；normal branch 则从同一次前向/反向中恢复 full gradient，投影到当前切空间的正交补上，得到 normal gradient，然后直接更新 base weights。这里有两个实现细节值得注意。其一，作者只对 normal branch 做 token-count normalization，即按输入位置数归一化梯度幅值，保持方向不变，目的是让不同序列长度或 token 数下的 normal update 更稳定。其二，base weights 不维护额外的 momentum / variance buffer，也就是不用 Adam 状态去追踪这条支路，从而避免像 FFT 那样为全量参数付出 optimizer-state 内存。这样做的取舍很明确：用更“轻”的 base update 换取部分 full-gradient 信息，而不是完全复制 FFT 的优化器行为。

和已有方法相比，差异也很清楚。Fira 试图用低秩投影近似 full-rank adaptive update，但需要周期性 SVD 或复用投影基，存在梯度子空间漂移问题。LoRA-GA、LoRA-Pro 则仍停留在 adapter 参数化内部，改善的是 LoRA 所诱导的权重梯度与 full gradient 的对齐程度。GDLoRA 直接承认当前 LoRA 切空间之外还有信息，并显式抽取这部分正交分量来更新 base weights，因此方法逻辑更直接。128:T95c,The method starts from a LoRA-injected linear layer with effective weight W_base + sBA. Given forward activations X and backward signals delta for the current batch, the unconstrained full weight gradient can be reconstructed as G_raw = delta^T X after flattening batch and token dimensions. The key theoretical result is that the set of equivalent weight-space gradients induced by Euclidean gradients on A and B coincides exactly with the tangent space of the current LoRA parameterization. This defines the LoRA-accessible gradient space.

Once this space is characterized, the full gradient can be orthogonally decomposed into a tangent component and a normal component. The latter is called the normal gradient. This component has two important properties. First, when nonzero, its negative is a local descent direction for the current batch loss when the current adapters and other parameters are held fixed. Second, it is orthogonal to every first-order direction available through the current LoRA factors, so it cannot be recovered merely by better initialization, rescaling, or re-optimizing the adapter gradients within the same parameterization.

GDLoRA uses two update branches. The adapter branch is standard LoRA optimized with AdamW. The normal branch reconstructs the full gradient from the same forward/backward pass, projects out the tangent-space component, and directly applies the remaining normal gradient to the base weights. A notable design choice is that token-count normalization is applied only to the normal branch, to stabilize update magnitude across different numbers of input positions while preserving direction. Another important choice is that the base weights do not maintain additional momentum or variance buffers. This is how the method avoids the optimizer-state overhead of FFT. In effect, GDLoRA supplements LoRA with a lightweight base-weight update that carries information unavailable to the current low-rank factors.

Compared with prior work, the distinction is clear. Fira approximates full-rank adaptive updates through projected gradients and periodically refreshed low-rank bases, which introduces basis-refresh trade-offs. LoRA-GA and LoRA-Pro improve how adapter gradients approximate the full gradient, but still remain inside the LoRA-induced update space. GDLoRA instead explicitly extracts the orthogonal complement and uses it directly.129:T5a4,The experiments span natural language understanding, mathematical and commonsense reasoning, and image classification. The main empirical claim is that under matched adapter and optimizer configurations, GDLoRA improves average performance by about 2% to 4% over standard LoRA and often approaches, or in some settings matches, full fine-tuning.

The emphasis on matched configurations matters. The paper is not claiming gains from extra trainable parameters or full optimizer states. It is testing whether the normal-gradient branch consistently adds useful information beyond what LoRA can express at first order. The most informative comparisons are therefore against standard LoRA, FFT, and methods such as Fira, LoRA-GA, and LoRA-Pro.

The ablations to pay attention to are the ones that isolate the mechanism: whether token-count normalization is necessary for the normal branch; how much is gained by combining LoRA updates with normal base-weight updates versus using either alone; how the method behaves at different ranks; and whether the benefit shrinks as rank increases. If the paper’s interpretation is correct, the gain should be more pronounced at lower ranks, where the LoRA tangent space is narrower and the normal component is more likely to contain important descent directions.

This is not a large-scale scaling-law paper. The value lies in making the missing-gradient story concrete, measurable, and empirically useful.12a:T4e1,Read this paper with one question in mind: is LoRA limited mainly by low-rank capacity, or by the restricted first-order update space of its current parameterization? Start with the introduction and the theorem-level characterization that the accessible gradient space equals the tangent space. That is the conceptual center of the paper. Then read the definition and properties of the normal gradient carefully, especially why it is a local descent direction and why it cannot be represented by first-order perturbations of the current LoRA factors.

After that, inspect the algorithm section to see that GDLoRA reuses signals already available from a standard backward pass rather than introducing an expensive second-order or repeatedly decomposed procedure. In the experiments, focus on the main comparison tables against LoRA and FFT, then the comparisons with Fira, LoRA-GA, and LoRA-Pro, and finally the ablations on token normalization, rank, and base-weight update design.

A 30-minute read is enough to capture the main idea. If you want to judge whether it is practical for large-model training, spend extra time on the appendix details about compute overhead, memory accounting, and how full-gradient recovery is implemented in practice.12b:T4e8,The paper uses Partial Information Decomposition to separate multimodal information into four channels. Redundant information R is accessible from either modality. Unique information U_1 and U_2 is accessible only from modality 1 or modality 2. Synergistic information S is accessible only when both modalities are present together. The proposed scaling law writes data loss as a sum of four independent power-law curves. Each curve receives only the relevant data stream: R can be reduced by either modality, U_1 by modality 1 data, U_2 by modality 2 data, and S only by the paired count n_p. This differs from prior L(N, D_1, D_2) forms because it gives paired data its own causal role rather than folding it into modality counts. The experimental protocol is built to isolate this variable. Unpaired examples are represented by a learnable null vector plus a modality-presence bit. At test time, both modalities are always present. Cross-entropy is the main loss, with accuracy checked separately. The main sweeps fix architecture and parameter count, folding finite-model effects into E_N, while appendices repeat Digits and VQA under different architectures and parameter sizes to check that the qualitative conclusions are not tied to a single model.12c:T5ca,The paper evaluates three settings. Digits combines MNIST images and AudioMNIST spectrograms in a four-digit classification task where the four positions correspond to U_1, U_2, R, and S, giving explicit control over the information channels. VQA trains classification heads on top of frozen pretrained embeddings; this setting is dominated by the text modality and is useful for observing how unpaired data helps non-synergistic information. NLVR2 finetunes a pretrained multimodal transformer on a task where mutual information is largely synergistic and unimodal models remain near chance. Across settings, the authors sweep total data D, compute budget C, paired count n_p, and multiple random seeds. They count D as D_1 + D_2, the sum of unique examples per modality. As p approaches 1, the number of unique rows decreases; training steps are fixed, so fully paired data sees more epochs but the same number of gradient updates. This counting convention favors unpaired data, making improvements from higher p more attributable to pairing itself. The main findings are consistent: pairing ratio has a large effect on loss; laws without p cannot capture the observed curves; only paired data reduces synergistic loss; unpaired data reduces redundant or unimodal loss only up to the relevant floors; and synergy shows a threshold-like acquisition pattern. The provided text does not include exact fit-error numbers for the proposed law, so no additional numeric claims are added.12d:T42e,The authors study an online teacher-student model with a single softmax layer trained by cross-entropy. Inputs are sampled from an isotropic Gaussian and RMS-normalized, mirroring hidden states before an LM head. A fixed teacher matrix produces hard one-hot labels from the argmax of its softmax output. The student learns with different optimizers. The setup preserves the key nonlinearity behind peaked distribution learning: reducing loss requires both growing the student weight norm, which sharpens the output distribution, and aligning the student direction with the teacher. The analysis decomposes the loss into a radial channel, controlled by norm growth and softmax saturation, and a tangential channel, controlled by directional misalignment. These channels decay with exponents α_r and α_t. SGD places both near one third. Adam produces a different dynamic regime, with α_r near one half and α_t near zero. inde","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"","category_id":"pretraining_data","cover_url":"/covers/2609_35869.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.AI","cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作讨论的是 tokenizer 里一个常被混在一起、但其实应当分开看的问题：预分词边界（通常由 regex 决定）到底让最优压缩损失了多少。过去很多工作会在“固定边界约束”下比较不同词表学习算法，然后得出 BPE 已经接近最优之类的结论；但这种结论只在受限可行域内成立，不能回答“如果允许 token 跨词边界，理论上还能少多少 token”。作者要解决的核心问题，就是给这个边界约束本身做一个可验证的、双边夹逼的压缩证书，而不是只比较某个具体 tokenizer 的经验结果。","importance":"对预训练研究的意义主要有两层。第一，它把 tokenizer 研究里“词表学习算法是否接近最优”和“边界约束本身值不值得保留”这两个问题拆开了。这个拆分很重要，因为很多关于 BPE、Unigram、无边界 tokenizer 的争论，实际是在比较不同优化问题。第二，它给出了一个可以独立验证的下界证书，使得“boundary tax”不再只是经验观察，而是有明确数值区间的优化量。对基座预训练来说，这直接关系到序列长度、训练 FLOPs、上下文利用率，以及 tokenizer 设计时压缩率和预测难度之间的取舍。论文后半部分又进一步说明：更短的 token 序列并不自动带来更好的 held-out 预测，这对“只看 token count 优化 tokenizer”是一个明确的纠偏。","technical_approach":"方法上，作者把最小 token 数分词写成一个带词表预算的整数规划。语料被表示成字节级 DAG：节点是字节位置，边是候选 substring 的出现位置；字节边永远可用，多字节边只有当对应字符串被选入词表时才可用。给定词表后，每个文档的最小 token 分词就是这个 DAG 上的最短路。难点在于，一个词表项一旦被选中，会同时激活它在全语料中的所有 occurrence，因此词表选择和具体分词路径是耦合的。\n\n作者的关键技巧是做 occurrence-level 的拉格朗日松弛：给每个候选 occurrence 一个非负价格 λ_e。这样，文档侧变成“带价格的最短路”，词表侧变成“收集某个 token 在所有 occurrence 上的总 bid”，再减去预算 K 下 top-K bid 的总和，就得到一个全局下界。这个形式有几个优点：一是不需要通用 LP 求解器，核心计算退化为每篇文档的 shortest path 加上全局 token bid 排序；二是价格可以近似优化，但证书有效性可以用独立的整数检查器验证；三是它既适用于 regex-constrained 语料，也适用于 unrestricted 语料，因此可以直接比较两种最优值，定义 boundary tax。\n\n除了两端点，作者还引入 boundary licence：允许有限数量的词表项跨越 regex cut。这样可以在“完全受限”和“完全无边界”之间画出压缩前沿，测量少量跨边界 token 到底能回收多少压缩收益。这一点比单纯比较两个端点更有分析价值，因为它把问题从二元选择变成了预算分配问题。\n\n论文还把压缩和预测分开评估。压缩侧看最优 token count 及其证书区间；预测侧则在明确的 vocabulary 和 decoder protocol 下做 held-out bits-per-byte 比较。作者强调，最小 token 数只是一个分词目标，不等于语言建模目标；无边界词表会改变 token 频率分布、上下文粒度和可预测性，因此需要单独测。","experiments":"核心结果有三组。第一，在 English Wikipedia 上，作者给出边界税的证书区间：regex 边界使最优 token 数增加 28.3% 到 36.8%。这个量级不小，说明预分词边界不是一个轻微工程细节，而是显著限制了压缩最优值。第二，BPE 相对“受边界约束的理论下界”只高 2.1%，说明在固定 regex 约束下，BPE 的压缩效率确实已经接近最优；但相对“无边界的理论下界”则高 10.9%，说明如果把问题定义改掉，BPE 离真正的全局最优并不近。这个结果很好地解释了为什么一边有人说 BPE 已经够好，另一边又有人通过放松边界拿到明显更短序列：他们比较的不是同一个 optimum。\n\n第三，作者做了 12 种语言的配对实验。结论是：无边界拟合出来的词典在压缩上更好，但测试集平均 bits per byte 在每种语言上都更高；用独立调参种子和评测种子复现实验后，这个方向在 12 种语言里保留了 11 种。也就是说，跨边界 token 虽然减少了步数，却往往让预测更难。论文把这点解释为词表内容、token 频率和有效字节上下文同时发生了变化。若从 LM 训练角度看，这意味着“更短序列”并不等于“更低 NLL”，甚至可能相反。\n\n从消融角度，boundary licence 前沿是值得注意的结果：它展示了允许少量跨边界词表项时，压缩收益如何逐步释放。这个实验帮助判断边界约束是否应当完全取消，还是只应当在有限预算下放松。虽然摘要里没有给出完整曲线数字，但从论文结构看，这部分是连接理论证书与 tokenizer 设计决策的关键。","reading_guide":"泛读时建议先抓三件事。第一，看 Introduction 和 Figure Most efficient attention methods impose a fixed sparsity pattern such as windows or block masks. That assumes a universal notion of locality across tokens, layers, and contexts. RoPE, on the other hand, gives a relative-position geometry but does not provide an explicit, controllable decay of relevance with distance. The key failure mode is that high-confidence tokens, especially near the end of a sequence, may be committed before the computations or context that support them have been resolved.","importance":"The contribution is most relevant to the practical decoding side of non-autoregressive and masked generative language models. MDLMs promise parallel generation, but that advantage depends on a reliable commitment policy. The paper shows that confidence alone is an insufficient criterion; commitment has to account for unresolved upstream dependencies. This is a useful signal for diffusion LM, masked LM, and any-order LM research, where decoding policy can decide whether the training-time parallelism becomes real inference speed.","technical_approach":"Reliable Parallel Decoding is a training-free decoding method. It uses two signals. First, it measures unresolved upstream uncertainty with cumulative entropy over masked upstream positions. If a downstream prediction depends on still-uncertain upstream information, RPD delays it. Second, it identifies tokens that can be committed together using layerwise stability: predictions that remain consistent across the final layers, without losing probability mass, are more likely to be correct. RPD selects candidates using stability and final confidence, then commits them under an entropy budget ordered by upstream uncertainty. This differs from fixed block-wise decoding, whose boundaries do not adapt to the current state, and from confidence or entropy thresholding methods, which score tokens without modeling whether their supporting context has been established.","experiments":"The evaluation uses LLaDA and Dream on mathematical reasoning and code generation, covering four benchmarks and eight model-task settings. The diagnostic study uses 2,000 gold arithmetic traces from GSM8K-Aug, masking upstream digits and final-answer digits under mask counts of 4, 8, 16, and 32, with 16 masking patterns per problem. One key observation is a U-shaped confidence profile: tokens near the end can look confident because of formatting priors rather than completed reasoning. Enforcing a better commitment order raises accuracy from 57.0% to 62.3% when the answer region is delayed, and to 72.0% when operands are required to precede dependent results. Its main idea is to use routing decisions as a discrete shared latent variable, turning an MoE backbone into a non-factorized reverse-process model without adding active parameters. This is a useful direction for pretraining research because it connects capacity scaling and generative factorization. The mixture index is a discrete latent variable given by the MoE router decisions across tokens and layers. Conditioned on a routing configuration, positions can still be sampled in parallel, but the shared routing state couples their predictions. During training, the same router evaluated on the noisy sequence acts as the generative prior, while the router evaluated on the clean sequence serves as the variational posterior. This removes the need for an extra recognition network and avoids imposing a fixed Gaussian prior. The paper derives an ELBO for this mixture-based reverse process and a tractable bound on the latent KL, reducible to per-layer and per-token router quantities. Compared with continuous-latent MDMs, the method reuses computation that the MoE model already performs and reduces the chance that the latent variable is silently ignored.","experiments":"The evaluation covers synthetic multimodal data, binarized MNIST, and LM1B. Deep-layer representations are not fed back to shallow layers, and the main channel for carrying information across generation steps is the sampled token. This narrow channel can force repeated computation and discard useful alternative continuations.","importance":"This is directly relevant to pretraining research because it changes the model’s information flow during pretraining, rather than adding only an inference-time controller. The main appeal is that it introduces a continuous recurrent state while preserving parallel training over sequence positions. It is a useful design point for latent reasoning and recurrent language modeling: keep the standard next-token objective, but add a supervised latent feedback channel that the model can consume at the next step.","technical_approach":"LIFT turns recurrent-state learning into a teacher-forced prediction problem. During training, each position receives both a token x_i and a state s_i, and the model is trained to predict the next token x_{i+1} and the next state s_{i+1}. The states are derived from the next-token distributions of an external pretrained teacher model. The teacher is used to supply informative input states during training, not merely soft targets for distillation. At inference time, the teacher is removed and the model feeds back its own predicted states. This differs from sequential latent-rollout methods, which are expensive to train, and from Jacobi-style feedback approximations, which require multiple parallel refinement iterations and therefore trade quality against training cost.","experiments":"The paper reports both controlled synthetic experiments and language-model pretraining runs. On S5 permutation composition, a state-tracking task known to be difficult for fixed-depth Transformers as length increases, two-layer vanilla Transformers fail at N≥12. Two-layer LIFT models solve 12-step sequences with 100% accuracy, even when the Transformer teacher providing states reaches only 3% accuracy at that length. For language modeling, LIFT models are pretrained from 135M to 1B parameters, with the 1B scale trained on up to 100B tokens, about five times the Chinchilla token budget. LIFT outperforms token-matched Transformers at every scale, and also beats distillation and Jacobi-iteration feedback baselines. Under compute-matched comparisons, it is comparable to or ahead of standard Transformers. The largest gains appear on procedural tasks such as multi-operand arithmetic and pattern continuation, where LIFT matches or exceeds Transformers trained on twice as many tokens.","reading_guide":"Plan for a 35–45 minute skim. The pretraining results should be read through token-matched and compute-matched comparisons, with attention to the cost of producing teacher states. 空间里不要塌缩到一起；Stability 要求 thought 反映的是可能输出的分布结构，而不是某一次采样答案的偶然痕迹。论文把这四点都写成可微损失，并与 CE 加权求和训练。\n\n实现上，作者把已有 latent recursive multi-agent 系统扩展到 single-agent 版本：单模型不再生成显式文本思维链，而是递归消费自己的 hidden states 作为下一轮 Long-context models can condition on hundreds or thousands of demonstrations, but pre-encoding those demonstrations produces KV tensors that grow linearly with the number of tokens. The paper focuses on how to store and reuse these demonstration caches efficiently, rather than on demonstration selection.","importance":"The work is primarily an inference-efficiency paper, not a pretraining method. Its relevance to foundation-model research is in the operating point it exposes for long-context models: if many-shot ICL becomes a common way to adapt models at inference time, the compressibility and fidelity of cached internal representations become part of the practical value of long-context pretraining. The paper treats redundancy in KV states as a structure that can be exploited, which is a useful lens for long-context model design and evaluation.","technical_approach":"The main method is block-wise low-rank compression of pre-encoded KV caches. MILO does not compress the entire many-shot context as one global matrix, because that can lose fine-grained information and add unnecessary decompression cost. It also avoids per-example compression, which fails to capture shared semantics across examples and can accumulate reconstruction error. Instead, it groups multiple demonstrations into a block and applies low-rank compression at that granularity. A second component is dynamic rank adaptation. Since different blocks have different information density, MILO estimates block entropy and assigns higher rank to high-entropy blocks while compressing redundant blocks more aggressively. The implementation includes custom kernels, CUDA graphs, and stream-level scheduling so that reduced storage translates into end-to-end latency improvements.","experiments":"The reported evaluation uses Qwen2.5 models on standard ICL benchmarks. 上，而是记录“已完成的 branch subgraph + 触发它的输入 + 它读过的外部依赖”。后续请求只有在输入精确匹配、且这些外部 reads 仍然新鲜时，才能消费该结果；一旦相关外部状态发生写入，就失效。这解决了 agent 工作流里 retrieval/tool 结果依赖外部环境、不能只靠 prompt exact match 复用的问题。\n\n第二层是 unresolved branch 的可寻址化。作者利用 workflow template 中在分支解析前就已知的 stable coordinate，也就是某个决策点在模板中的身份，例如 router stage、某个固定工具选择位点。借助这个坐标，系统可以在分支尚未真正解析时，先为若干候选分支启动 fills。这里的 fill 可以理解为“在 resolution window 内预跑的候选子图执行”。关键约束是：这些 speculative fills 在分支真正选定前对外不可见，只有当后续 canonical demand 到来，并且 exact match 与 freshness 都满足时，才会被提升为可用结果。因此错误预测只会浪费资源，不会改变语义结果。\n\n第三层是 admission control。作者设计了两级在线控制器：一级决定要不要生成候选分支，二级决定每个候选 fill 是否执行。控制依据是 expected benefit 是否超过 load price。这个 price 不是静态阈值，而是读取当前引擎 decode 占用和 KV 占用，按 fill 的执行时间窗动态定价。这样在低负载时更积极地做 speculation，在高负载时自动收缩，避免 speculative work 抢占 canonical 请求资源。文中还提到控制器从延迟反馈中在线学习收益估计，而不是只靠固定启发式。\n\n系统实现上，DynBranch 部署在 model-API boundary，位于 agent harness 与 SGLang/vLLM 之间，因此不要求修改底层模型执行引擎，也不要求 agent 框架配合改写。这一点决定了它更像一个 serving middleware，而不是新的 agent runtime。","experiments":"实验设置以 Qwen3-32B、4×H200 为主，也补充了 Qwen3-8B/RTX 4090 的 commodity 环境。作者声称在四类 agent workload 和生产 trace 上评估了 branch-resolution barrier 的占比，并指出在测得的 backbone family 上持续存在，说明方法依赖的是 workflow 结构和 serving 时序，而不是某个模型特性。\n\n由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格，无法可靠补充更多 workload 级别的绝对延迟、命中率、控制器 ablation 数字；但从摘要和引言可确认，核心结论是“reuse + early fill + load-aware Channels with slow decay retain quantization noise for many steps, while fast-decaying channels dissipate it quickly. Uniform range-based quantization therefore allocates precision without considering the future impact of the error.","importance":"The main value for pretraining and architecture work is the connection between hybrid-LM state dynamics and inference-time memory efficiency. Models such as Kimi Delta Attention, Gated DeltaNet, and Mamba-2 replace part of the attention cache with fixed-size recurrent states, shifting the systems bottleneck toward state storage, read/write bandwidth, and numerical precision. The paper provides a data-free, training-free, rotation-free allocation rule for recurrent-state quantization. It also makes a broader point: KV-cache quantization heuristics are not directly sufficient for recurrent architectures, because state errors have temporal dynamics. This can inform future choices of decay parameterization, state grouping, normalization, and quantization-friendly architecture design.","technical_approach":"The method assigns a distortion weight to each state channel using an observability Gramian. Under a local linear noise model, steady-state readout MSE can be approximated as sum_i Gamma_i sigma_i^2, where sigma_i^2 is the quantization noise variance for a row and Gamma_i measures how strongly that row’s error will be observed in future outputs. For diagonal decay without erasure, the paper derives Gamma_i = rho_i / (C expm1(2 s_i)), where s_i is the decay rate, rho_i is query-weighted energy, and C is the write-back interval. Slow decay therefore receives higher precision. These weights are combined with normalized state ranges inside output-normalization groups and plugged into a classical high-rate mixed-precision bit-allocation rule. Decay rates are quantized uniformly in log s, reflecting the sensitivity of long time constants to small relative changes in decay.","experiments":"The experiments evaluate three hybrid models and seven baselines. With per-token recurrent-state quantization, a 4-bit mean payload reduces excess negative log-likelihood by factors of 3.3 to 27.9 relative to the best baseline. At 6 bits, the NLL gap to the FP32-state baseline is below 0.005 nats. The paper includes ablations separating the contributions of variable bit widths, decay-aware weighting, range normalization, and logarithmic decay-rate quantization. It also reports an important caveat: deterministic rounding at C=1 can create correlated errors. In simulations using Kimi-like decays and rank-one writes, lag-one error correlations reach 0.23 for very slow channels, and three-to-five-bit readout error can range from 0.17x to 2.4x the independent-noise prediction. By six bits, discrepancies are typically within 20%. The Gramian rule is therefore best read as a robust allocation heuristic, not as an exact error model.","reading_guide":"A useful skim should take about 25–35 minutes. In the experiments, focus on the 4-bit and 6-bit NLL comparisons, metadata overhead, and the ablation table. Along time, every decoding step updates an already quantized state and quantizes it again; retention gates can carry old errors forward. The method therefore uses lifetime-aware bit allocation, assigning more precision to state units whose errors are both large and long-lived under a fixed memory budget. Along space, errors in different key rows have different impact on the output, while state magnitudes vary across both rows and columns. The proposed key-row-aware dual-axis fitting assigns separate scales to key rows and value columns. Row scales account for magnitude and output sensitivity; column scales are fitted with higher weight on rows where errors matter more. This differs from uniform, per-tensor, or single-axis quantization because it is designed for a continuously updated memory matrix rather than a static weight tensor.","experiments":"The evaluation uses Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct on seven long-generation and six short-generation tasks. Its 4-bit setting outperforms uniform INT8; it nearly matches FP32-state performance on Qwen and keeps a smaller but visible gap on Kimi. Standard calibration reconstructs fixed image-text contexts, while deployment follows prefixes produced by the quantized model itself. A single quantization-induced token change can redirect the prefix and alter all future states. The paper also makes a useful distinction: on-policy coverage alone is not sufficient, because many next-token discrepancies have little downstream effect. That framing is relevant to distillation, RL post-training, synthetic data filtering, and long-chain reasoning stability. It first rolls out the current quantized policy and collects the states actually visited at deployment time. At each shared quantized prefix, both the dense model and the quantized model are queried, which isolates next-token decision changes at the same state. The method then identifies mismatches and near-miss decision boundaries, runs short counterfactual rollouts from competing tokens, and estimates how far the resulting futures separate. Boundary erosion, same-state distribution discrepancy, and branch consequence are combined into a Decision-Consequence risk used to weight calibration. A static context anchor is kept to preserve broader multimodal behavior. After each calibration update, trajectories are refreshed under the updated quantized policy. The paper also derives a bound that decomposes behavioral deviation into current policy discrepancy and the future value span conditioned on alternative actions.","experiments":"The experiments cover multiple VLM backbones and quantization settings. 级别不加载某些专家，输出会发生变化。论文把某个专家被移除造成的层输出误差写成平方范数形式，其中既包含单专家 removal term，也包含多个被同时移除时的 cross terms。作者的关键判断是：在实际选择中，忽略 cross terms 仍能较稳定地得到接近最优的 batch expert set，因此可以把每个专家的贡献独立打分，再在固定预算下保留分数最高的专家。\n\n具体分数来自“预测的移除误差”。对某个 token-专家对，若移除专家 u，误差近似与 router weight 的平方以及该专家输出能量 ||E_u(z_t)||^2 相关。难点在于真正的 expert output 只有把专家权重取回并执行后才知道，而 batch 选择恰恰发生在此之前。BASE token 上限。这样做不是为了省算力，而是为了让后面的“语义压缩提示”只在局部、语义相对一致的范围内工作，避免整篇文档过长时重要性估计过于噪声。\n\n第二步，在每个 chunk 末尾追加一个很短的 semantic compression prompt，例如 “Brief summary: \\\"”。这个 prompt 的作用不是生成摘要文本，而是诱发模型在预测 prompt 后续 token 时，把注意力集中到 chunk 中更关键的内容上。作者特别说明结尾的冒号和引号是为了减少模型把下一个 token 预测成标点，从而让注意力模式更像语义压缩而不是格式续写。\n\n第三步，设计 prompt-isolated attention mask。这个 mask 做了两件事：一，后续文档 token 不允许去看这些插入的 prompt，避免 prompt 污染原始文档 token GPTQ uses a calibration Hessian H=XX^T and quantizes columns sequentially, compensating future columns after each rounding decision. Since output rows are independent under the same input Hessian, each row follows its own recurrence. For each hardware-valid block scale, Schur Replay replays the GPTQ updates that this candidate scale would induce, then scores the block with a conditional Schur objective that accounts for the remaining compensation available from unquantized columns. This differs from static block-scale search, which evaluates scales before the candidate has changed the GPTQ state.
